# Blueprint

84 tools. Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_ai_perception_sense`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Configure a sight or hearing sense on an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint, creating the config as an Instanced subobject of the template so it persists with the asset, and saving the package. Idempotent: ConfigureSense dedups by config class, so re-calling with the same sense_type UPDATES the existing config in place instead of stacking a second one. Only "sight" and "hearing" are supported (no damage, touch or team senses). It authors the TEMPLATE only -- whether the AI actually perceives anything is a live-PIE question this cannot answer; read the authored result back with get_ai_perception_senses.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint owning the component |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of the AIPerceptionComponent SCS node |
| `sense_type` | string | yes | "sight" or "hearing" |
| `dominant` | boolean | no | Optional bool; if true, sets this sense as the component's dominant sense |
| `sight_radius` | number | no | (sight) Maximum sight distance, cm (ClampMin 0) |
| `lose_sight_radius` | number | no | (sight) Distance to keep seeing an already-seen target, cm (ClampMin 0) |
| `peripheral_vision_angle` | number | no | (sight) Peripheral vision half-angle, degrees (Clamp 0..180) |
| `hearing_range` | number | no | (hearing) Hearing range, cm (ClampMin 0) |
| `detect_enemies` | boolean | no | Optional bool affiliation filter |
| `detect_neutrals` | boolean | no | Optional bool affiliation filter |
| `detect_friendlies` | boolean | no | Optional bool affiliation filter |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, component_name, sense_type, config_class, <sense fields>, note }`

## `add_blueprint_function`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Create a NEW function graph on a Blueprint, or with override=true a real OVERRIDE of an inherited/interface member: an event-shape member (no return value) becomes a genuine event OVERRIDE node in the event graph (node_id returned, placed at node_position), a value-returning one a real override FUNCTION graph (in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs for an interface member) -- the only correct route for interface events, since a hand-placed event node can compile yet never fire. The override is idempotent (was_already_overridden) and leaves the Blueprint needing a compile, unsaved. It REFUSES rather than guessing: a name that collides with an overridable inherited function errors with a hint instead of silently creating a "&lt;name>_0" shadow, and an EVENT-shape member already shadowed by a local function graph errors telling you to remove that graph first. The new graph does not exist in the generated class until compile_blueprint, so compile BEFORE add_function_parameter or any node that calls it -- otherwise a build_blueprint_graph step fails with "Function not found" and rolls the whole batch back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint (for override=true it must already implement the interface / inherit the virtual; implement_interface first). |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name for the new function; with override=true, the EXACT name of the inherited (interface or parent-class) function to override (e.g. "CanInteract", "GetInteractText"). |
| `override` | boolean | no | Optional. When true, create an OVERRIDE of an inherited function ('My Blueprint > Override'): resolves the interface/parent-virtual signature and creates the override graph (function-shape) or event override node (event-shape) with the inherited signature + exact name -- NOT a new deduped function. When omitted and the name collides with an inherited overridable function, the call errors with a hint (instead of silently making a '&lt;name>_0' shadow); pass override=false to force a brand-new function anyway. |
| `node_position` | array | no | Optional [x, y] canvas position for an event-override node that override=true CREATES (an existing one is not moved; a function graph has no single node to place). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, function_name: string, graph_name: string, success: bool [, kind, already_existed, created, was_already_overridden, node_id, already_exists, is_interface_function, note] } -- with override=true: kind='function' (graph_name is an editable function-override graph, ready to wire with get_graph_nodes / connect_pins) or kind='event' (an event OVERRIDE node was created or reused in the event graph graph_name names, and node_id is that node); created is !already_existed, and was_already_overridden is already_existed. success:true can come back WITHOUT the graph actually appearing, so confirm with get_blueprint_functions before wiring it.`

## `add_blueprint_variable`

*Additive.*

Add a MEMBER variable to a Blueprint (add_function_local_variable is the function-scoped twin), then read/write it with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set. TRAP 1: the variable is born NOT editable per instance -- placing the actor and writing that variable fails with "cannot be edited on instances" -- and get_blueprint_variables reports instance_editable:true anyway; fix it with set_blueprint_variable_metadata(instance_editable=true). TRAP 2: on a class that ALREADY has actors placed in a level, those instances keep the value of the first compile, so a default set afterwards never reaches them -- verify on the instances, not on the CDO.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | New variable name (fails if the name already exists on this Blueprint). |
| `variable_type` | string | yes | Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, or the name/path of a struct, enum, class or object (e.g. Vector, /Game/Dir/S_Foo.S_Foo, /Script/Engine.Actor). |
| `is_array` | boolean | no | When true, make the variable an array container; defaults to false. This is the ONLY array authoring path -- add_function_parameter has no equivalent. |
| `default_value` | string | no | Initial default value for the new variable, in exported-text form; optional |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, variable_type, is_array } -- an echo of the request, NOT a verification: read the variable back with get_blueprint_variables (or the CDO) before relying on it.`

## `add_broadcast_node`

*Additive.*

Add the node that BROADCASTS (fires) an event dispatcher on self -- own or inherited -- with one input pin per signature parameter, so listeners run. Does NOT compile. The dispatcher must already exist in the compiled class (add_event_dispatcher then compile_blueprint), and its parameter pins only appear after set_event_dispatcher_signature. The opposite direction (LISTENING) is add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" for self, add_object_bound_event for another object's dispatcher.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint that owns (or inherits) the dispatcher |
| `dispatcher_name` | string | yes | Exact name of the multicast delegate to broadcast; resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited dispatchers work |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, one input per signature param], blueprint_name, graph_name, dispatcher_name } -- an empty parameter list means the dispatcher has no signature yet.`

## `add_comment_node`

*Destructive.*

Add a resizable comment box (UEdGraphNode_Comment) to a graph. KNOWN BUG: the 'text' parameter is LOST -- the comment is assigned before the node is finalized and the engine's PostPlacedNewNode then overwrites it, so every box created this way reads "Comment"; the returned "comment" field is the oracle and there is no MCP way to fix it (write the rationale in the system's docs instead, and delete the empty box). It also has NO pins, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at it breaks a whole build_blueprint_graph batch.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `text` | string | no | Comment text; currently IGNORED (see the bug above), the box always ends up saying "Comment" |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `width` | number | no | Comment box width in pixels; defaults to 400 |
| `height` | number | no | Comment box height in pixels; defaults to 200 |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment } -- no pins array. comment=="Comment" means the requested text was not written.`

## `add_component_bound_event`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Bind a multicast delegate OF ONE OF THIS BLUEPRINT'S OWN COMPONENTS (OnComponentBeginOverlap, OnComponentHit, a vendor component's dispatcher...) to a generated handler event in the event graph -- the editor's component-event flow -- then compile and re-check that the binding registered (bound). ALSO WORKS ON A WIDGET BLUEPRINT: pass the WBP and a WIDGET's name as component_name to wire a Button's OnClicked, a Slider's OnValueChanged, a CheckBox's OnCheckStateChanged -- exactly what the Designer's "+ OnClicked" green button does, and the only headless route to it (bound:true, with a BndEvt__..._OnButtonClickedEvent created). A UMG widget is not an SCS component but IS a property of the generated class, which is all this needs. Idempotent: an identical binding is returned instead of duplicated. The Blueprint must already be compiled, since the component/widget has to exist as a property of the generated class. For a dispatcher on an object that is NOT self and NOT one of its components, use add_object_bound_event; for one on SELF, add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate".

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint OR a Widget Blueprint (already compiled). |
| `component_name` | string | yes | SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (e.g. "BodyMesh"), OR -- on a Widget Blueprint -- the name of a widget in its tree (e.g. "Btn_Play"); resolved on the skeleton class, so inherited components and widgets work too. |
| `delegate_name` | string | yes | Exact multicast delegate property name on the COMPONENT's class (e.g. "OnComponentBeginOverlap"). On a miss the error names the component class so the right delegate can be looked up. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[...the delegate's params as OUTPUT pins...], blueprint_name, graph_name, component_name, delegate, custom_function_name, bound, already_exists? } -- bound is a post-compile re-lookup (the real oracle); already_exists is only present when an existing binding was reused.`

## `add_component_to_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Add a component of any class (engine class or a Blueprint AC_* class) to a Blueprint's SCS, with an optional relative transform and parent, then compile. Pick it to change the Blueprint so every instance gets the component; add_component_to_actor adds one to a single placed actor only, and attach_blueprint_component re-parents a component that already exists. TRAP 1: on a CHILD Blueprint whose scene root is INHERITED, a SCENE component can end up written into the PARENT's SCS (source:"inherited", owner_class = the parent) -- which silently edits a vendor/library asset; non-scene ActorComponents land correctly on the child. TRAP 2: a scene component of a BLUEPRINT class, or one given a location, can report success without persisting and then materialize LATER as a duplicate. Both have the same oracle: get_blueprint_components right after, checking owner_class and source of the new node -- never the return value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_type` | string | yes | Component class: a native short name ('StaticMesh', 'Box', 'Sphere'), a /Script path ('/Script/Engine.StaticMeshComponent'), OR a Blueprint component class given as its object path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo.AC_Foo_C'), a bare package path ('/Game/.../AC_Foo'), or a bare '&lt;Name>_C' ('AC_Foo_C'). |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name for the new component instance |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative location for scene components |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] relative rotation for scene components |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] relative scale for scene components |
| `transform` | object | no | Optional {"location":[x,y,z], "rotation":[p,y,r], "scale":[x,y,z]} alias for scene components; any flat location/rotation/scale arg above wins over the matching axis in here if both are given. |
| `parent_component_name` | string | no | Optional parent for scene components; omit / "root" attaches under the Blueprint's EXISTING scene root (SCS or native) instead of force-adding a second orphan root node. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0"), mirroring attach_blueprint_component. Ignored for non-scene ActorComponents (no transform, no hierarchy to join). |
| `socket_name` | string | no | Optional socket/bone name on the parent (AttachToName) |

**Returns:** `{ component_name: string, component_type: string } -- an ECHO of the request with no owner, no source and no verification. It says nothing about WHERE the node landed: read get_blueprint_components afterwards.`

## `add_enhanced_input_action_node`

*Additive.*

Add an Enhanced Input action event node (UK2Node_EnhancedInputAction) bound to a UInputAction asset. Unlike add_input_action_event_node -- which creates the LEGACY UK2Node_InputAction that does NOT fire under Enhanced Input -- this node exposes the real ETriggerEvent exec pins (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) that fire from the Enhanced Input pipeline. Use this instead of polling IsInputKeyDown in a timer; it is rebind-aware (bound to the InputAction asset, not a raw key).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of an Actor/Pawn Blueprint. |
| `input_action` | string | yes | Asset path (or short name) of the UInputAction to bind, e.g. "/Game/Input/IA_Crouch". |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pins:[{name, direction, type, linked_to, default}], blueprint_name, graph_name, input_action, node_class } -- the created node WITH its freshly-allocated pins: ETriggerEvent exec outputs (Triggered/Started/Ongoing/Canceled/Completed) plus data outputs (ActionValue/ElapsedSeconds/TriggeredSeconds/InputAction). Wire it via connect_pins WITHOUT a follow-up get_graph_nodes.`

## `add_event_dispatcher`

*Additive.*

Create an event dispatcher (multicast delegate) on a Blueprint: adds BOTH the delegate member variable and its signature graph, the way the editor's "+ Event Dispatcher" does. It starts with NO parameters -- give it a signature with set_event_dispatcher_signature. Everything downstream needs the class REGENERATED first, so compile_blueprint before add_broadcast_node (to fire it) or add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate" / add_object_bound_event (to listen).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `dispatcher_name` | string | yes | Name of the new event dispatcher; fails if a member variable of that name already exists |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, created } -- created is always true on success; confirm with get_event_dispatchers.`

## `add_function_local_variable`

*Additive.*

Add a variable scoped to ONE function graph (interface-override graphs included), instead of a class member like add_blueprint_variable -- use it for scratch state that no other graph should see. Reach it from the graph with add_graph_node node_type=variable_get/variable_set and scope="local" (the default scope="auto" already prefers a local over a member of the same name).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph) |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Variable name; the call fails if the name already exists in that function |
| `variable_type` | string | yes | Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path |
| `default_value` | string | no | Initial default value for the local variable, in exported-text form; optional |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, variable_name, variable_type } -- an echo of the request; local variables do NOT appear in get_blueprint_variables (which lists members), so verify from the graph itself.`

## `add_function_parameter`

*Additive.*

Add an input or output (return) parameter to an existing Blueprint FUNCTION graph -- interface-override graphs included -- and reconstruct its Entry/Result node. TWO HARD LIMITS, both silent-ish: it cannot create an ARRAY parameter (there is no is_array; the param comes out SCALAR with success), so redesign the signature to read the array where it lives; and it cannot reach a CUSTOM EVENT ("Function graph not found"), so a Server/Client RPC WITH arguments must be authored as a function plus set_blueprint_function_rpc. On a Blueprint just given a new function, compile_blueprint between creation and this call.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing function graph (FunctionGraphs or an interface-override graph). A custom event is NOT a function graph and is rejected here. |
| `param_name` | string | yes | New parameter name; made unique, so the applied name is the one echoed back in the response. |
| `param_type` | string | yes | Type string: bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, or a struct/enum/class/object name or path. Arrays are NOT expressible. |
| `is_output` | boolean | no | When true, add an output/return param (an input pin on the Result node) instead of an input; defaults to false |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, param_name, param_type, is_output } -- param_name is the pin name actually created (uniquified). Verify with get_graph_nodes at compact=false: compact hides the new, still-unlinked pin and makes it look like nothing was created.`

## `add_graph_node`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create ONE node in a Blueprint's event/function graph (node_type selects the kind) and return it WITH its freshly allocated pins, so connect_pins / set_pin_default_value can wire it immediately without a follow-up get_graph_nodes; with compile=true it also compiles the Blueprint afterwards. Use build_blueprint_graph instead when several nodes must be created AND wired in a single undo transaction, and get_function_pins to learn a call_function's pin names BEFORE creating anything. node_type='event' creates a REAL override (the declaring interface/parent class is resolved automatically and bOverrideFunction is set; target_class is ignored here; an existing override is returned with already_exists:true) and fails loudly for a name that is not an overridable event -- an interface method WITH a return value is not an event, use add_blueprint_function with override=true. node_type='custom_event' is idempotent by name (an existing custom event of that name in the graph comes back with already_existed:true, since a second one breaks the compile); a custom event cannot be given parameters, so anything that needs arguments (an RPC in particular) must be a function. node_type='get_component_by_class' makes a GetComponentByClass node BORN TYPED to target_class, so its ReturnValue connects without a cast -- inside build_blueprint_graph a generic one would be connected before its class pin default is applied and fail.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name (resolved under /Game/Blueprints) or full asset path. Pass the FULL path when the short name is ambiguous: a bare name that matches two assets resolves to one of them silently. |
| `node_type` | string | yes | One of event, custom_event, call_function, print_string, variable_get, variable_set, branch, sequence, self, cast, spawn_actor (alias spawn_actor_from_class), create_widget, make_struct, break_struct, get_array_item, select, make_array, make_set, make_map, switch_int, switch_string, switch_name, switch_enum, enum_literal, format_text, foreach, foreach_with_break, do_once, gate, flipflop, for_loop, while_loop, is_valid, add_delegate, macro_instance, get_component_by_class |
| `event_name` | string | no | Event name; required for event and custom_event node types (e.g. "ReceiveActorBeginOverlap", "ReceiveBeginPlay" for event) |
| `function_name` | string | no | Function to call; required for call_function node type |
| `target_class` | string | no | Class owning the function or cast/spawn target class; required for cast, create_widget and get_component_by_class. For call_function it is searched STRICTLY: a function that is not on that class is an error, never a silent fallback to another library; it also resolves a user BlueprintFunctionLibrary by asset path ("/Game/Dir/BFL_X"). For get_component_by_class it is the component class to fetch (a UActorComponent subclass). For variable_get/variable_set it names the class that owns the variable, producing a non-self member-access node (with a 'target' pin) instead of a self-context node. For create_widget it names the widget class to construct (e.g. WBP_Foo_C, a full asset path, or the widget Blueprint short name); the node exposes that widget's Expose-On-Spawn pins. |
| `function_library` | string | no | Optional, call_function only: the library class owning function_name, used instead of target_class -- an engine library by name ("KismetMathLibrary", "KismetSystemLibrary", "GameplayStatics", "KismetStringLibrary", with or without the U prefix, or any /Script/Engine class) or a user BlueprintFunctionLibrary asset path ("/Game/Dir/BFL_X", "/Game/Dir/BFL_X.BFL_X" or the "..._C" class). Searched strictly, like target_class. |
| `variable_name` | string | no | Variable to get/set; required for variable_get and variable_set |
| `scope` | string | no | Optional scope hint for variable_get/variable_set: 'auto' (default; a function-local variable declared in the target graph wins, else a self/member variable), 'local' (function-local variable ONLY), or 'member' (member variable only -- self, or on target_class when supplied). Ignored by other node types. |
| `struct_type` | string | no | Struct type; required for make_struct and break_struct nodes: a UScriptStruct path (/Game/.../S_Foo.S_Foo), bare name, or engine alias (Vector/Rotator/Transform...) |
| `enum_path` | string | no | Enum path or name; required for switch_enum and enum_literal nodes. Optional for select: the enum then drives the Index pin and one option pin is generated per enum entry. |
| `index_type` | string | no | Optional alias of enum_path for node_type=select. |
| `option_count` | number | no | Optional, select only: total number of option pins to end up with (default the built-in 2; ignored when an enum drives the index). |
| `num_inputs` | number | no | Optional input-pin count for make_array/make_set/make_map (added after spawn) |
| `cases` | string | no | Optional string array of case pins for switch_int/switch_string/switch_name |
| `arguments` | string | no | Optional string array of argument names for format_text |
| `dispatcher` | string | no | Event-dispatcher (multicast delegate) name; required for add_delegate node type. Must already exist in the COMPILED class (add_event_dispatcher + compile_blueprint), and it binds on self only -- for a dispatcher on another class use add_object_bound_event. |
| `macro_graph_name` | string | no | Macro graph name; required for node_type=macro_instance. Resolved against this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs first, then the engine StandardMacros; "&lt;library-path>:&lt;MacroGraphName>" (e.g. "/Game/Lib/ML_X.ML_X:MyMacro") resolves it in that macro library instead. |
| `macro_library` | string | no | Optional, macro_instance only: asset path of a macro LIBRARY Blueprint to resolve macro_graph_name in -- the only way to reach a third-party or project macro library. |
| `macro_source` | string | no | Set to "standard_macros" to skip this Blueprint's own MacroGraphs and resolve macro_graph_name only in the engine StandardMacros library. Only read for node_type=macro_instance. |
| `compile` | boolean | no | Optional bool, default false: compile the Blueprint after placing the node. Ignored inside build_blueprint_graph, which never compiles its steps. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[{name, direction:'input'|'output', type, linked_to, default}], blueprint_name, graph_name, compiled, event_name?, node_title?, already_existed?, is_override?, already_exists?, cast_to?, function_library?, function?, struct_type?, index_pin?, return_value_pin?, option_pins?, option_count?, index_enum?, input_pins?, output_pins?, component_class?, return_pin_type? } -- the created node WITH its freshly-allocated pins. The pin names are already here, so you can wire the node via connect_pins/set_pin_default_value WITHOUT a follow-up get_graph_nodes. The optional fields belong to their node_type: event_name/node_title/already_existed for custom_event; event_name/is_override/already_exists for event (is_override:true is what tells a live override from a dead look-alike); cast_to for cast; function_library/function for call_function; struct_type for make_struct/break_struct; index_pin/return_value_pin/option_pins/option_count/index_enum for select; input_pins/output_pins (pin names by direction) for macro_instance; component_class/return_pin_type for get_component_by_class (return_pin_type is the oracle: if it does not name the requested class, the pin stayed generic). Read "class" as a sanity check: a node_type that was expected to produce an async/latent node and comes back as "K2Node_CallFunction" is a mute no-op that still compiles 0/0.`

## `add_input_action_event_node`

*Additive.*

Add the LEGACY action-mapping event node (UK2Node_InputAction) bound to an action mapping NAME, and compile. WARNING: this node does NOT fire under Enhanced Input, which is what UE5 projects use -- it compiles clean and simply never runs. For an Enhanced Input action asset use add_enhanced_input_action_node, whose Triggered/Started/Completed pins actually execute. Only reach for this one on a project still using the legacy input mappings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of an Actor/Pawn Blueprint (SupportsInputEvents is enforced). |
| `input_action_name` | string | yes | Name of the LEGACY action mapping. It is not validated against the project's mappings: a typo yields a node that never fires. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[Pressed, Released, Key], blueprint_name, graph_name, input_action_name, node_class } -- node_class should read K2Node_InputAction (the legacy node); nothing here proves the mapping exists.`

## `add_object_bound_event`

*Additive.*

Bind a BlueprintAssignable event dispatcher of an EXTERNAL object (not self, not a component) to a handler custom event -- the editor's right-click "Assign" flow (FEdGraphSchemaAction_K2AssignDelegate). Use this to react to a dispatcher on a widget/actor instance held in a variable (e.g. a UMG widget's "On Radial Menu Item Selected"): it spawns a UK2Node_AddDelegate bound to target_class' dispatcher with its self/target pin LEFT UNCONNECTED (you wire the instance) and a UK2Node_CustomEvent whose OUTPUT pins mirror the dispatcher's params (e.g. the segment-data struct), already wired to the AddDelegate's Delegate pin. Unlike the add_delegate node_type (self-context only), this reaches a dispatcher on a foreign class. Does NOT compile the Blueprint (mirrors the engine action); compile afterward.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint being edited (the object that will bind the event, e.g. the hub component BP). |
| `target_class` | string | yes | The EXTERNAL class that owns the dispatcher. Accepts a Blueprint/widget short name, a full asset path, a full class path (/Game/.../WBP.WBP_C), a native /Script path, or the generated "..._C" class name. Prefer a full path or the "_C" class for reliable resolution. |
| `dispatcher_name` | string | yes | The multicast delegate (event dispatcher) property to assign. Matched tolerantly: exact name, spaces stripped, or the display name (so "On Item Selected" resolves to the spaceless FName). On failure the error lists the assignable delegates found on target_class. |
| `event_name` | string | no | Optional desired name for the handler custom event; made unique in the Blueprint. Defaults to "&lt;Dispatcher>_Event". |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, graph_name, target_class, dispatcher, add_delegate_node_id, custom_event_node_id, custom_event_name, wired, node_id, pins:[...] (the AddDelegate node's pins -- wire 'self'/Target = the widget instance and 'execute'/'then' into your exec flow), custom_event:{ node_id, pins:[...] } (hang handler logic off its 'then'/'output_delegate' and read the dispatcher's param output pins) }`

## `add_parent_call_node`

*Additive.*

Add a "Parent: &lt;Function>" node that calls the parent-class implementation of an overridden function/event -- the second half of the child-first shape "Event X -> Parent: X -> our logic" that keeps a vendor base class working while the child adds behaviour. Searches the WHOLE ancestor chain, not just the immediate parent. Does NOT compile, and IS allowed inside build_blueprint_graph, so the event + super + logic can be built in one transaction.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint whose parent function is called |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the overridden function/event whose parent implementation to call; must exist on some ancestor or the call errors |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph (usually the override's own graph); defaults to the event graph |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[execute, then, the parent's params], blueprint_name, graph_name, function_name, parent_class } -- parent_class names the ancestor that actually declares the implementation being called.`

## `add_reroute_node`

*Additive.*

Add a reroute/knot node: pure layout, it re-emits whatever is wired into it and changes no behaviour. Does NOT compile. Note when reading graphs back: get_graph_nodes with compact=true excludes knots by default, so a chain that looks broken there may simply route through one -- re-read with exclude_classes=[].

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[...wildcard in/out until wired...], blueprint_name, graph_name }`

## `add_timeline_to_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Add a Timeline to an Actor Blueprint: creates BOTH the UTimelineTemplate variable and its UK2Node_Timeline node in one call, sets a fixed length in seconds, compiles, and verifies the template really registered (timeline_created). Actor-derived Blueprints only. It does NOT author curves or tracks -- the node comes with Play/Stop/Reverse inputs and Update/Finished outputs and nothing driven; a requested name already in use is silently uniquified, so wire the RETURNED timeline_name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint. |
| `timeline_name` | string | yes | Desired variable name for the timeline; if it is taken, a unique one is generated and returned instead. |
| `length` | number | no | Timeline length in seconds (sets fixed-length mode); defaults to 5.0 |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, class, title, pins:[...], blueprint_name, graph_name, timeline_name, length, timeline_created, timeline_guid } -- timeline_name is the name ACTUALLY used and timeline_created is a post-compile re-lookup of the template, so false means the variable did not survive.`

## `apply_material_to_blueprint`

*Destructive.*

Assign a material ASSET to one slot of a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor) -- the persistent counterpart of set_mesh_material_color, which only builds a runtime dynamic instance. Does NOT compile and does NOT save. Actors ALREADY placed in a level keep their serialized material: change the template and the placed instances stay as they were.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent |
| `material_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMaterialInterface (material or material instance) to assign; a path that does not load is an error |
| `material_slot` | number | no | Optional material slot index; defaults to 0. It is not range-checked against the mesh's slot count. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_path: string, material_slot: int, success: bool } -- an echo: success:true only means the material loaded and SetMaterial was called. Read it back with get_blueprint_material_info.`

## `attach_blueprint_component`

*Destructive.*

Parent an existing SCS component under another component (or the native root). The parent may be an SCS component of this Blueprint OR a NATIVE inherited scene component from a parent C++ class (e.g. ACharacter's "CharacterMesh0" or the native capsule) -- when the name is not an SCS node and is not the native root, it is resolved from the parent-class CDO and the child is parented to it natively (bIsParentComponentNative=true). This makes sockets on inherited native meshes reachable (e.g. a socket under CharacterMesh0 at "spine_4", or a ChildActor attached at "spine_2").

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of the SCS component to attach (the child) |
| `parent_component_name` | string | no | Optional parent component name; omit / "root" / the native root name attaches to the native root component. May also name a NATIVE inherited scene component (e.g. "CharacterMesh0") to parent the child natively to it. |
| `socket_name` | string | no | Optional socket/bone name on the parent (AttachToName) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, component_name, parent, parent_is_native, attach_socket, already_attached }`

## `build_blueprint_graph`

*Destructive.*

Build several nodes, wire their pins, and set pin defaults in one pass, wrapped in a single undo transaction -- the way to author a whole graph shape without create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips (get_function_pins gives you the pin names up front). THE ORDER IS FIXED AND MATTERS: every node first, then ALL connections, then pin_defaults -- so a node whose TYPE depends on a pin default (a generic GetComponentByClass) is connected while still untyped, fails with "... is not compatible with ..." and, under stop_on_error's default true, takes the whole call down; use add_graph_node node_type="get_component_by_class", which is born typed. add_comment_node has no pins at all, so a pin_defaults entry aimed at one also kills the batch. Self-contained: each sub-step runs its command directly, never through the bridge (only these: add_graph_node, add_timeline_to_blueprint, add_component_bound_event, add_input_action_event_node, add_enhanced_input_action_node, add_reroute_node, add_comment_node, add_parent_call_node, add_broadcast_node, add_object_bound_event), and no step compiles: an add_graph_node step's compile param is ignored, so compile_blueprint once afterwards.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `nodes` | array | yes | [{id: string, command_type: string, params?: object}, ...] (required, non-empty). 'id' is a caller-chosen local key used to reference the node from 'connections'/'pin_defaults'; 'params' is that command's own param object (blueprint_name/graph_name are auto-filled if omitted). WORKED EXAMPLE (print "hi" on BeginPlay, one call): nodes=[{"id":"beg","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"print","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"print_string"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"beg","from_pin":"then","to_node":"print","to_pin":"execute"}], pin_defaults=[{"node":"print","pin":"InString","value":"hi"}]. Pin names for a call_function node are knowable up front via get_function_pins (so no create->get_graph_nodes->connect round-trips). Child-override canonical shape (call the parent first), one call: nodes=[{"id":"evt","command_type":"add_graph_node","params":{"node_type":"event","event_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}},{"id":"super","command_type":"add_parent_call_node","params":{"function_name":"ReceiveBeginPlay"}}], connections=[{"from_node":"evt","from_pin":"then","to_node":"super","to_pin":"execute"}]. NOTE on add_object_bound_event: it creates TWO nodes; the step's local 'id' resolves to the UK2Node_AddDelegate (wire the external instance into its 'self' pin and the exec flow into 'execute'), while the handler custom event is addressable as "&lt;id>.custom_event" and its real NodeGuid is echoed back as custom_event_node_id. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `connections` | array | no | [{from_node, from_pin, to_node, to_pin}, ...]; from_node/to_node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "&lt;id>.custom_event" for an add_object_bound_event step's handler event) or a pre-existing real NodeGuid. |
| `pin_defaults` | array | no | [{node, pin, value}, ...]; node may be a local 'id' from 'nodes' (or "&lt;id>.custom_event") or a pre-existing real NodeGuid. |
| `stop_on_error` | boolean | no | Stop (and try to roll back the whole transaction) on the first failing step; defaults to true, unlike batch's default false, since connections/pin_defaults depend on earlier nodes existing. With stop_on_error:false there is NO rollback at all -- the editor's global undo is never touched, every step is attempted, and whatever half-built shape remains is cleaned up with delete_node/disconnect_pin. That is the safer mode when other work is live in the editor's undo buffer. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes: [{index, id, command_type, ok, node_id?, custom_event_node_id?, error?}], connections: [{index, ok, error?}], pin_defaults: [{index, ok, error?}], stopped_early, rollback_required, rolled_back, transaction_opened, undo_queue_len_before, undo_queue_len_after, top_transaction_title, rollback_refused_reason?, warning? }. rolled_back reports whether the undo ACTUALLY ran, not the intention: the rollback is refused (rolled_back:false + rollback_refused_reason + warning) whenever the top of the editor's undo stack is not this call's own transaction, because GEditor->UndoTransaction is global and would otherwise revert another agent's or another session's work in memory while the disk stays clean. A payload that fails pre-validation returns instead { success:false, error, validation_errors: [{section, index, id?, error}], transaction_opened:false, blueprint_name, graph_name } and never opens a transaction.`

## `compile_blueprint`

*Destructive.*

Compile a Blueprint to regenerate its class, returning the REAL outcome (succeeded == zero errors) plus the error/warning counts, and with return_messages=true the per-message log with each message anchored to its node_id/graph. Required after authoring functions, variables or RPCs and before anything calls them. TRAP: num_errors:0 is not a promise the graph works -- an unresolved WILDCARD pin on an array/ForEach node can compile clean and still block PIE, and warnings (a "was pruned" node whose consumers silently read defaults) do not lower it, so read the warnings too. Compiling dirties the package and can cascade into other packages; check_blueprint_errors / find_erroring_blueprints answer without a compile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint, or its full asset path (e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor). A short name matching two assets compiles ONE of them silently -- pass the full path when in doubt. |
| `return_messages` | boolean | no | Optional (default false). When true, ALSO returns the per-message compiler results log so callers can see node-anchored errors/warnings. When false/absent the response omits the `messages` array but still reports the REAL compile status. |

**Returns:** `` { name: string, compiled: bool, succeeded: bool, num_errors: int, num_warnings: int } -- `compiled`/`succeeded` reflect the ACTUAL compile outcome (true iff zero errors; warnings still compile). Both the default and return_messages paths return these fields. When return_messages=true additionally { messages: [{severity: 'error'|'warning'|'note', text: string, node_id: string, node_title: string, graph_name: string}] } (node_id/node_title/graph_name are empty strings when the message is not anchored to a graph node) ``

## `connect_pins`

*Destructive.*

Wire one node's OUTPUT pin to another node's INPUT pin inside one Blueprint graph, type-checked by the K2 schema (an incompatible pair is returned as an error, never a silent no-op). Nodes are addressed by NodeGuid, pins by name. Either node that still carries a WILDCARD pin is reconstructed afterwards, so array / ForEach / Select pins really re-type instead of compiling into "The type of Target Array is undetermined" (which compile_blueprint reports as compiled:true). Use validate_pin_connection to test a pair without mutating, and build_blueprint_graph to create+wire in one transaction.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `source_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the source node (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes). |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Output pin name on the source node (e.g. "then", "ReturnValue"). An output pin of that name is preferred; any pin with the name is accepted as a fallback. |
| `target_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target node. |
| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin name on the target node (e.g. "execute", "Condition"). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. BOTH nodes must live in this same graph. |

**Returns:** `{ connected, source_node_id, target_node_id } -- connected is always true when the call succeeds; the failure path is an error response, so there is no false to check.`

## `create_blueprint`

*Additive.*

Create a new Blueprint asset, optionally as a child of ANY parent class -- native or another Blueprint (pass its "..._C" class or asset path) -- and save it to disk immediately unless PIE is running or save=false. This is also the way to make the framework classes (a GameMode, GameState, PlayerController, PlayerState, GameInstance or HUD Blueprint: pass that class as parent_class) and Blueprint subsystems (parent_class a USubsystem class such as "GameInstanceSubsystem"; lifetime says which family), and it makes Blueprint Function Libraries and Macro Libraries, which have no Actor parent and which the normal path would reject. It does NOT create interfaces (create_blueprint_interface). A plain Blueprint already at the path is returned unchanged with already_exists=true and saved=false, nothing saved and blueprint_type not applied -- when parent_class is given, only if its parent is parent_class or derives from it, otherwise it is an error and nothing is changed; another asset class there (a Widget or Anim Blueprint included) is an error and nothing is created. It never confirms the parent of a new Blueprint: read it back with get_blueprint_parent.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Blueprint name. Either a bare name (created under 'path' or /Game/Blueprints/) OR a full content path ("/Game/MyGame/Systems/World/BP_Foo"); an object-path form ("/Game/.../BP_Foo.BP_Foo") is also accepted. |
| `parent_class` | string | no | Optional parent class. Accepts a native name ("Actor", "Pawn", "Character", "GameModeBase", "PlayerController", "GameInstanceSubsystem", "BlueprintFunctionLibrary"), a "/Script/Module.Class" path, a Blueprint generated-class path ("/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C"), or a Blueprint asset path ("/Game/.../BP_X"). Defaults to AActor. Passing "BlueprintFunctionLibrary" makes a Function Library. When given, a Blueprint already at the path must have it (or a subclass of it) as parent. |
| `blueprint_type` | string | no | Optional Blueprint type override: "normal" (default), "function_library" (a UBlueprintFunctionLibrary of static functions; parent_class is ignored/forced), or "macro" (a Macro Library; keeps parent_class or defaults to Actor). Function-library is also auto-detected from parent_class="BlueprintFunctionLibrary". |
| `path` | string | no | Optional target content folder ("/Game/MyGame/Systems"). Used only when 'name' is a bare name; ignored when 'name' is already a full path. |
| `save` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). false registers the new Blueprint and marks its package dirty without saving it -- persist it later with save_asset. |

**Returns:** `{ name: string, path: string, package_path: string, parent_class: string, generated_class: string, blueprint_type: string, already_exists: bool, saved: bool (false for a Blueprint already there: nothing saved), save_error?: string, note?: string, is_multiplayer?: bool, lifetime?: string } -- parent_class is, for a new Blueprint, what was REQUESTED and resolved, not proof the asset carries it (confirm a child's real parent with get_blueprint_parent), and for one already there its own parent. is_multiplayer appears for a GameMode (true when the parent derives from AGameMode); lifetime for a subsystem (Editor, Engine, GameInstance, World, LocalPlayer or Unknown). saved:false is honest: it carries save_error when PIE was running or the Blueprint already there has unsaved changes, and a note when save=false or an existing Blueprint is returned unchanged -- an unsaved Blueprint exists only in the editor and a later compile on it also returns success.`

## `create_blueprint_macro`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an EMPTY, Tunnel-terminated macro graph owned by this Blueprint's MacroGraphs (a reusable snippet, not a function: macros inline at compile time and can carry multiple exec outputs). Idempotent -- an existing macro of that name is returned with already_existed:true. Fill it with add_graph_node using graph_name=&lt;macro>, then instantiate it with add_graph_node node_type="macro_instance", which finds the Blueprint's own macros.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `macro_name` | string | yes | Name for the new macro graph. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, macro_name, graph_name, already_existed } -- graph_name is what to pass as graph_name / macro_graph downstream.`

## `create_editor_utility_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an Editor Utility Blueprint at package_path/name with the editor factory, parented to parent_class, then compile and save it. Idempotent by path: an Editor Utility Blueprint already there is returned as it is (created=false, already_existed=true, saved=false), nothing compiled or saved, with the parent_class it really has; the requested parent_class is not applied to it. A parent_class that does not resolve or cannot back a Blueprint, another kind of asset at that path, or an invalid path is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the new asset in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. A tool with a UI panel: create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint. Right-click actions are made here too: parent_class "AssetActionUtility" (Content Browser assets) or "ActorActionUtility" (level actors) -- their CallInEditor functions become the actions.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored. |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUB_BatchRename". |
| `parent_class` | string | no | Parent class by name without the U or A prefix, e.g. "EditorUtilityActor", or by path such as "/Script/Blutility.EditorUtilityObject" (default EditorUtilityObject); it must be Blueprintable. |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, created, already_existed, saved, save_error? }`

## `create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint at package_path/name with the editor factory, parented to UEditorUtilityWidget, give it a CanvasPanel root named RootCanvas when the factory made no root, then compile and save it. Idempotent by path: an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint already there is returned as it is (created=false, already_existed=true, saved=false), nothing compiled or saved, with the parent_class and root it really has. Another kind of asset at that path, or an invalid path, is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false with save_error and keeps the new asset in memory. Refused during PIE unless force=true. Open it as a tab with run_editor_utility_widget; find them with list_editor_utility_widgets; a plain Widget Blueprint is create_widget_blueprint.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_path` | string | yes | Content folder for the asset, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities"; a trailing slash is ignored. |
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name without path or extension, e.g. "EUW_LevelTools". |

**Returns:** `{ name, package_path, asset_path, blueprint_class, parent_class, root_widget, root_widget_class, created, already_existed, root_created, saved, save_error? }`

## `delete_blueprint_variable`

*Destructive.*

Remove a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused) and report whether it is really gone by re-looking it up. Nodes that still read/write it survive as broken references, so run compile_blueprint with return_messages=true afterwards. For an event dispatcher use remove_event_dispatcher instead -- this call would drop the delegate variable and strand its signature graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, deleted } -- deleted is re-checked after the removal, so false means it is still there.`

## `delete_node`

*Destructive.*

Delete ONE node from a graph by its NodeGuid, breaking its links; refused for nodes the editor protects (FunctionEntry, Result, tunnels). This is the cleanup for orphan nodes left behind when a build_blueprint_graph batch fails and its rollback is refused, and it is reversible (the .uasset on disk is untouched until save_asset). It does NOT compile -- follow with compile_blueprint with return_messages=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node to delete |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ deleted, node_id }`

## `disconnect_pin`

*Destructive.*

Break ALL links on one pin of one node (there is no way to drop a single link of a multi-linked pin). Main use: clearing links that point at nodes which no longer exist after a failed or refused build_blueprint_graph rollback -- get_graph_nodes with compact=false shows those as linked_to entries with dead GUIDs. To remove the whole node instead, use delete_node.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node owning the pin (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes) |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | Pin name, in either direction |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ disconnected, node_id, pin_name }`

## `find_blueprint_node_references`

*Read-only.*

"Find in Blueprints" over MCP: locate every Blueprint NODE that references a symbol -- variable, function, event, custom event, multicast delegate, macro, timeline, cast target, component, or a class/object in a pin default -- across a content path, returning each hit's asset, graph chain, node_id, title, match_kind and RESOLVED declaring class (resolved:false = a name-only guess). READ-ONLY. THE RULE FOR READING A ZERO: matches_found:0 only measures NON-EXISTENCE when `assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match` comes back EMPTY -- if it names assets, the symbol's string IS in those packages, so either the real name is spelled differently or the reference lives outside a graph (component template, property default). Check coverage_complete too: a truncated, timed-out or capped scan proves nothing. Blind by construction: Level Script Blueprints inside a .umap, and C++ callers.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | string | no | Required (unless component_name is given): the name to look for, matched EXACTLY (variable/function/event/macro/class/component name). A misspelling returns 0 with a full-coverage report -- see assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match before believing it. |
| `component_name` | string | no | Optional: search for an actor COMPONENT by name; implies mode="component" and, with owner_blueprint, also matches GetComponentByClass/Cast pins that target the component's class. |
| `owner_blueprint` | string | no | Optional: Blueprint that DECLARES component_name (asset name or path); required to resolve the component's class for the class-pin matching. |
| `mode` | string | no | Optional (default "auto"): auto\|all\|variable\|function\|event\|delegate\|macro\|component\|class\|pin_default. Filters which match kinds are returned; an unrecognized value returns everything and sets mode_recognized=false. |
| `path` | string | no | Optional (default "/Game"): content path root to scan. |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): recurse into subfolders of path. |
| `exclude_paths` | array | no | Optional: array of package-path prefixes to skip (e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/Demo"]). |
| `include_paths` | array | no | Optional: array of package-path prefixes to restrict the scan to (applied after path). |
| `prefilter` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): byte-scan the .uasset name map before loading. Turning it OFF loads every Blueprint under path (slow, but the ground truth to compare against). |
| `case_sensitive` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): case-sensitive symbol matching (both the byte prefilter and the node classifier). |
| `include_pin_defaults` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): also report pin defaults / pin types that name the symbol, on nodes with no structural match. |
| `include_node_json` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): embed the full NodeToJson serialization of each matching node. |
| `include_pins` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): when include_node_json is on, include the node's pins. |
| `max_assets` | number | no | Optional (default 20000): hard cap on candidate assets examined. |
| `max_matches` | number | no | Optional (default 200): stop after this many matches (sets truncated=true). |
| `max_seconds` | number | no | Optional (default 60): wall-clock budget; on expiry the scan stops and timed_out=true. |

**Returns:** `{ symbol, mode, mode_recognized, path, recursive, prefilter_enabled, component_class, component_declared_in, assets_in_path, assets_scanned, assets_prefiltered_out, assets_prefilter_unavailable, assets_prefilter_bypassed_dirty, assets_loaded, assets_load_failed, assets_with_matches, graphs_visited, nodes_visited, foreign_subgraphs_skipped, matches_found, truncated, timed_out, coverage_complete, elapsed_ms, assets_hit_prefilter_without_graph_match:[string], notes:[string], matches:[{asset_name, asset_path, package_name, graph, graph_chain, graph_kind, node_id, node_class, node_title, match_kind, member_name, declaring_class, resolved, is_component_ref, is_interface_call, exact, detail, pin, pin_value, node?}], success }`

## `fork_class_chain`

*Destructive.*

One-call thin-fork + optional reparent + verify: collapses the create->reparent->verify pattern into a single call. It creates a NEW thin child Blueprint of base_class at fork_name (the seam you insert between a shared-library base and your own class), optionally tags it with the fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag), saves it, and then -- only if reparent_target is given -- reparents that existing Blueprint onto the new fork through the guarded reparent_blueprint path (snapshot + compile flags + post-check + rollback) and reports its verification. WARNING: no durable backup is taken -- the rollback is in-memory only, so call backup_asset yourself first if you want a rollback-to-disk safety net.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fork_name` | string | yes | Name or full /Game path for the NEW thin child Blueprint to create. |
| `base_class` | string | yes | Parent class for the new fork (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path). |
| `path` | string | no | Optional folder for fork_name when it is a bare name (default /Game/Blueprints). |
| `fork_origin` | string | no | Optional: value stored in the fork's fork-origin metadata tag (project setting ForkOriginTag, default 'mcp.forkOrigin'), recording its fork lineage. |
| `reparent_target` | string | no | Optional: an existing Blueprint to reparent onto the new fork. |
| `auto_rollback` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target. |
| `rename_colliding_vars` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): forwarded to the safe reparent of reparent_target. |

**Returns:** `{ fork_name, fork_path, fork_generated_class, base_class, already_exists, fork_origin_set, saved, save_error?, reparent:{...safe-reparent result...}|null, verification, verification_checks, error?, success }`

## `get_actor_material_info`

*Read-only.*

List the material slots of an actor PLACED IN THE EDITOR WORLD, one row per slot per StaticMeshComponent, with the material actually assigned (name, path, class) or "None". Scope limits worth knowing: it only walks UStaticMeshComponents (a skeletal mesh's slots are invisible here) and only the EDITOR world (no PIE selector), and the actor is matched by its object NAME, not its outliner label. The Blueprint-template twin is get_blueprint_material_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Object name of the actor in the EDITOR world (GetName(), not the display label shown in the outliner) |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int } -- total_slots 0 means no StaticMeshComponent had slots, NOT that the actor has no materials.`

## `get_ai_perception_senses`

*Read-only.*

Read back the senses configured on an AIPerceptionComponent TEMPLATE of a Blueprint: for each one its config class plus the fields that matter (sight radius / lose-sight radius / peripheral angle, or hearing range) and the three affiliation filters. This is the verification step for add_ai_perception_sense. It reads the OWN SCS template, so an AIPerception component inherited from a parent Blueprint is not found, and a config class other than Sight or Hearing comes back with sense_type "unknown" and no fields.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint owning the component |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS AIPerceptionComponent node; another component type is an explicit error |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, component_name, senses: [ { config_class, sense_type, sight_radius|hearing_range, ... , detect_enemies, detect_neutrals, detect_friendlies } ], sense_count } -- sense_count 0 means the template has no configured sense, which is also what an AI that never perceives anything looks like.`

## `get_available_materials`

*Read-only.*

Enumerate material assets under a content path and return each one's name, object path, package and class -- the object path is what apply_material_to_blueprint / set_actor_material expect. One Asset Registry query on UMaterialInterface and all its subclasses (materials, material instances, project or plugin material classes); nothing is loaded, so a wide path is cheap. For one known name prefer resolve_asset_by_name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search_path` | string | no | Optional content path filter (e.g. "/Game/Materials"); empty/absent means the whole project and is reported back as "/Game/" |
| `include_engine_materials` | boolean | no | When true, also include /Engine/ materials; defaults to true, so the list is large unless a search_path narrows it |

**Returns:** `{ materials: [{ name, path, package, class }], count: int, search_path_used: string } -- there is no truncation flag: count is everything that matched.`

## `get_blueprint_component_object_path`

*Read-only.*

Resolve a Blueprint component's TEMPLATE archetype and return its object path, so get_properties/set_properties/call_function can target that component directly.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name/path of the Blueprint that owns the component. |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component variable name. Resolves an OWN SCS component (the _GEN_VARIABLE archetype on USCS_Node::ComponentTemplate) or an INHERITED/native component (the like-named subobject on the generated-class CDO). |

**Returns:** `{ object_path: string, class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited' } -- object_path is GetPathName() (feed it to get_properties / set_properties); class is the component class' full path.`

## `get_blueprint_component_property`

*Read-only.*

Read the EFFECTIVE default of a property (or, without property_name, ALL properties) on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE as typed JSON, resolving components INHERITED from a parent/grandparent Blueprint. Use it instead of get_component_properties with blueprint_name, which sees only own SCS nodes and native subobjects, not inherited SCS components or their ICH overrides. Order: own SCS template -> nearest existing ICH override -> ancestor's declaring SCS template -> native CDO subobject; source says which. NEVER mints an ICH override. group_by_field flags duplicate keys in an array of structs. Write: set_blueprint_component_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset path or short name |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component variable name (own or inherited) |
| `property_name` | string | no | Property to read; omit to return ALL properties of the resolved template |
| `include_inherited` | boolean | no | Also resolve inherited/ICH/native components (default true); when false only this Blueprint's own SCS components are considered |
| `group_by_field` | string | no | Optional. Only with property_name pointing at a TArray of STRUCTS: group the elements by this struct member and report duplicate_groups[]/empty_key_indices[]/has_duplicates. Two elements sharing a key is invisible in a plain value dump, yet when that array feeds a TMap the LAST one silently wins (Map.Add overwrites) -- this is the guardrail for exactly that class of bug. |
| `report_duplicates` | boolean | no | Optional bool. Implied true when group_by_field is given; pass true WITHOUT group_by_field to group by the WHOLE element value instead of one member. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, source: 'scs'|'inherited-ich'|'inherited-scs'|'inherited-native', resolved_from_class: string, property_name: string, value: any (single-property mode), properties: object, property_count: int (all-properties mode), duplicate_analysis?: { grouped_by, element_count, distinct_keys, duplicate_groups: [{key, count, indices[]}], empty_key_indices: [int], has_duplicates: bool, keys: [string] } }`

## `get_blueprint_functions`

*Read-only.*

List the graphs of a Blueprint -- functions, interface implementation graphs, macros, delegate signatures and, on request, event graph pages -- each with its node count, a REAL is_override (resolved against the parent class chain AND every implemented interface, naming the declaring class) and is_pure (read off the graph's FunctionEntry FUNC_BlueprintPure flag, not guessed). Enumerates the FULL graph set (UBlueprint::GetAllGraphs), not just Blueprint->FunctionGraphs: an INTERFACE override graph lives in ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs, which FunctionGraphs alone misses (a function that exists would read as "missing"). Each entry carries graph_type so the caller can tell a plain function from an interface override, a macro or a delegate signature. The map to read before get_graph_nodes, which needs an exact graph name. WARNING: graph_type 'event_graph' entries are the TRANSIENT compiled event graphs and are absent on a Blueprint not compiled this session -- the authored EventGraph is the 'ubergraph' page. get_class_functions has the compiled class surface (inherited and native functions included).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint, or its full path. A bare name that matches more than one Blueprint asset (a backup copy shares the original's name) resolves to one of them and lists the others in `ambiguous_matches` -- pass the full path then. |
| `filter_type` | string | no | Optional 'all' (default), 'functions' or 'events' (case-insensitive, singular accepted). 'functions' keeps function, interface, macro and delegate_signature graphs; 'events' keeps the event side (ubergraph pages and compiled event graphs) and lists it without include_ubergraphs. |
| `include_ubergraphs` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): also list the event side -- the authored EventGraph/ubergraph pages (graph_type='ubergraph') and the transient compiled event graphs (graph_type='event_graph'). Off by default so 'functions' stays function-shaped. |
| `include_macros` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): list MacroGraphs (graph_type='macro'). |
| `include_interface_graphs` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): list ImplementedInterfaces[].Graphs (graph_type='interface'). |
| `include_subgraphs` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): also list nested/collapsed sub-graphs reached by GetAllGraphs but owned by no top-level list (graph_type='subgraph') |
| `max_results` | number | no | Optional maximum number of entries to return, 1..10000 (default 1000); results_truncated says whether any were left out. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string], filter_type: string, functions: [{ name, node_count, graph_type, is_interface, interface_name?, interface_class?, is_user_constructed, is_pure?, is_override?, override_declaring_class? }], function_count: int, override_count: int, own_function_graph_count: int, interface_graph_count: int, macro_graph_count: int, delegate_graph_count: int, ubergraph_count: int, event_graph_count: int, subgraph_count: int, graphs_total: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool } -- graph_type is function|interface|macro|delegate_signature|ubergraph|event_graph|subgraph; is_pure/is_override are on function, interface and macro entries (a macro is neither), override_declaring_class names the class or interface (path) that declares what is overridden; is_user_constructed is just node_count>2, i.e. "someone wrote something beyond the auto Entry/Result terminators", because implementing an interface pre-creates empty graphs. The *_count totals count every graph of that kind, listed or not: subgraph_count>0 with include_subgraphs off is the warning that collapsed graphs exist and are not listed.`

## `get_blueprint_info`

*Read-only.*

One cheap overview of a Blueprint: parent class, compile status, and the counts + names of its OWN components, variables, function graphs and ubergraph pages. Everything here is what THIS asset declares -- nothing inherited, and interface-override graphs are not listed. So use it to orient, and the specialists to decide: get_blueprint_components for the real component set including ancestors, get_blueprint_functions for interface/macro/delegate graphs, get_blueprint_variables for variable flags, get_graph_nodes to read a graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, parent_class: string, components: [{ name, type }], component_count: int, variables: [{ name, type }], variable_count: int, functions: [{ name }], function_count: int, graphs: [{ name, type }], graph_count: int, has_event_graph: bool, event_graph_name?: string, status: string } -- parent_class is a short NAME (ambiguous between an engine class and a same-named project one), variable "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (no struct/class), and status is UpToDate/Error/Unknown.`

## `get_blueprint_material_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the material slots of ONE StaticMeshComponent TEMPLATE in a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node), with the material assigned to each slot or "None". This is the verification step after apply_material_to_blueprint / set_static_mesh_properties. The slot count comes from the assigned static mesh's LOD 0 sections, so with no mesh assigned it returns ZERO slots and has_static_mesh:false -- which is a missing mesh, not a missing material. For a placed actor use get_actor_material_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS component; it must be a UStaticMeshComponent (any other type is an error) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, component_name: string, material_slots: [{ slot, component, material_name, material_path, material_class }], total_slots: int, has_static_mesh: bool } -- read has_static_mesh FIRST: total_slots:0 with has_static_mesh:false means no mesh was assigned, so the array says nothing about materials.`

## `get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info`

*Read-only.*

Read ONE variable's full detail: its default value, the structured type (category, sub-category object and container kind -- not just the pin category get_blueprint_variables gives you), and every checkbox of the variable Details panel -- is_instance_editable / is_expose_on_spawn / is_blueprint_read_only / is_expose_to_cinematics / is_replicated / replication_condition / save_game. This is the headless oracle for "does this variable really persist into a .sav?", which otherwise costs a co-op PIE session plus a binary grep of the slot file. save_game is reported from BOTH places the flag lives, because they disagree until you compile: `save_game` is CPF_SaveGame as AUTHORED (FBPVariableDescription::PropertyFlags, exactly what the editor checkbox writes) while `save_game_generated` is the same flag on the FProperty of the GENERATED class, which is the one the save archive consults -- so save_game:true + save_game_generated:false means MARKED BUT NOT COMPILED, and nothing will persist yet; `save_game_matches` says it in one field. Read is_replicated FIRST: replication_condition is always populated (COND_None by default) and only means anything when replication is on. `default_value` is read from the CDO when the class is compiled (`default_value_source:"cdo"`), so it does not come back EMPTY for arrays, maps and every variable of an already-compiled Blueprint. Booleans of this family are contrasted, not believed -- audit_replication is the ground truth for replication.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (e.g. "MyFloat"); inherited variables are not covered |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, variable_name: string, default_value: string, default_value_source: "cdo"|"blueprint_description", default_value_serialized: string, var_type: string, property_type: string, var_type_detail: {category, sub_category, sub_category_object, sub_category_object_path, container}, is_instance_editable: bool, is_expose_on_spawn: bool, is_blueprint_read_only: bool, is_expose_to_cinematics: bool, is_replicated: bool, replication_condition: string, save_game: bool, save_game_generated: bool, save_game_generated_found: bool, save_game_matches: bool }`

## `get_blueprint_variables`

*Read-only.*

List the variables this Blueprint DECLARES (its NewVariables) with name, pin category, editor category, tooltip and the flags that matter for co-op and UI work: is_public (BlueprintVisible), is_editable, is_blueprint_read_only, is_replicated (CPF_Net) and is_expose_on_spawn. Inherited variables, native C++ UPROPERTYs, function locals and components are NOT here -- get_class_properties on the generated class (..._C) has the full property surface. THE FLAGS ARE READ OFF THE STORED VARIABLE DESCRIPTION, not the compiled property, and two of them mislead: is_editable checks CPF_Edit and ignores CPF_DisableEditOnInstance, so it says true for variables the editor refuses to edit per instance; is_expose_on_spawn checks a property flag while set_blueprint_variable_metadata writes the ExposeOnSpawn METADATA, so it says false for variables that DO show up as SpawnActor pins. Oracles: write the placed instance for editability, the spawn node's pins for exposure, get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info for type/replication and one variable's default value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint, or its full path. A bare name that matches more than one Blueprint asset resolves to one of them and lists the others in `ambiguous_matches`. |
