| `max_results` | number | no | Optional maximum number of variables to return, 1..10000 (default 1000); results_truncated says whether any were left out. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, blueprint_path: string, blueprint_valid: bool, ambiguous_matches?: [string], variables: [{ name, type, category, tooltip, is_public, is_editable, is_blueprint_read_only, is_replicated, is_expose_on_spawn, instance_editable, expose_on_spawn }], variable_count: int, variables_count: int, max_results: int, results_truncated: bool } -- "type" is only the pin CATEGORY (e.g. "struct", "object"), not the struct or class; instance_editable and expose_on_spawn repeat is_editable and is_expose_on_spawn; variable_count and variables_count are the same number.`

## `get_event_dispatchers`

*Read-only.*

List a Blueprint's event dispatchers (multicast delegates) WITH each one's full parameter signature (name, C++ type, is_output) and whether it is inherited. Read from the SKELETON class, so it reflects edits made since the last full compile. Use it before add_broadcast_node / add_object_bound_event / set_event_dispatcher_signature, whose pins mirror this signature; only the dispatchers this Blueprint DECLARES can have their signature edited.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `include_inherited` | boolean | no | Also include dispatchers inherited from parent classes; default false = only the ones this Blueprint declares (i.e. the editable ones) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, dispatchers: [ { name: string, is_inherited: bool, param_count: int, params: [ { name: string, type: string, is_output: bool } ] } ], dispatcher_count: int }`

## `get_function_pins`

*Read-only.*

Preview the EXACT pins an add_graph_node call_function node WOULD expose for a UFunction WITHOUT creating anything: owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input/exec_output ("execute"/"then", null when pure), self_pin (null when static), input_params, output_params and return_value. This is what lets a whole build_blueprint_graph (nodes + connections + pin_defaults) be written in ONE call instead of create -> get_graph_nodes -> connect round-trips. It answers "what pins would it have", NOT "can a Blueprint call it": some engine functions resolve and preview here and are still rejected by the compiler, so the oracle for callability is compile_blueprint with return_messages=true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `function_name` | string | yes | UFunction name, matched EXACTLY against the reflected name (e.g. "PrintString", "K2_GetActorLocation", or a Blueprint function graph's own name, which may contain spaces like "Emit Noise At Location"). A guessed name that does not exist just errors -- it never returns an empty preview. |
| `target_class` | string | no | Optional class searched FIRST: native name ("KismetSystemLibrary"), "/Script/Module.Class", a Blueprint class path ("/Game/...X_C"), or a user BFL. Also always searched: the blueprint's own class + KismetSystem/GameplayStatics/KismetMath. |
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Optional Blueprint whose generated class joins the search (for self / BP-local functions). |

**Returns:** `{ function_name, owner_class, is_pure, is_static, exec_input, exec_output, self_pin, input_params:[{name,type}], output_params:[{name,type}], return_value:{name,type}|null, note }`

## `get_graph_nodes`

*Read-only.*

Read one Blueprint graph: every node with its node_id (NodeGuid), class, title, position, comment and pins (name, direction, type, linked_to, default) -- the read that feeds connect_pins / set_pin_default_value / delete_node, and the way to see what a graph actually DOES. TRAP: compact=true drops per-pin type metadata AND omits every pin that is unlinked and default-less (plus knots and comment boxes), so a pin missing from a compact listing is NOT proof the pin does not exist -- re-read with compact=false before concluding anything about pins. Also: a bare blueprint_name that matches two assets picks one silently (pass the full path), and reading a graph under a read-only vendor root leaves that package DIRTY in memory (reload_asset_package with on_dirty="discard" cleans it).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path. Prefer the FULL path: a short name with more than one match resolves silently to one of them, and stale backup copies share the original's name. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. Also resolves a collapsed composite subgraph by its title (e.g. 'In Game HUD') and accepts a path form ('EventGraph > In Game HUD'). |
| `expand_composites` | boolean | no | When true, inline the nodes of collapsed composite subgraphs recursively; each node gains a "graph" tag naming the graph it came from. Macro-library graphs are never inlined. (Optional, default false) |
| `compact` | boolean | no | Token-lean listing: drops pin types, positions and comments, and skips pins that are unlinked AND have no default. Also excludes K2Node_Knot + EdGraphNode_Comment unless exclude_classes is given. Good for reading topology, WRONG for checking whether a pin exists. (Optional, default false) |
| `exclude_classes` | array | no | Array of leaf node class names to skip, matched against each node's "class" field (e.g. ["K2Node_Knot"]). Pass [] to include everything even in compact mode. Absent + compact=true means knots and comments are excluded; absent + compact=false excludes nothing. |
| `max_nodes` | number | no | Cap on the number of nodes emitted (&lt;=0 or absent = unlimited); the response still counts every non-excluded node in total_node_count and sets truncated=true. |
| `node_id` | string | no | Optional NodeGuid (from add_graph_node / get_graph_nodes): return ONLY that node of the graph, always at full fidelity (compact, exclude_classes, expand_composites and max_nodes are ignored) -- every pin with name, direction, type, linked_to and default, at a fraction of the tokens of a whole graph. A node_id the graph does not contain is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, graph_name, nodes:[{node_id, class, title, pos_x, pos_y, comment, pins:[...], subgraph?}], node_count, compact, total_node_count, excluded_count, truncated } -- node_count is what was EMITTED, total_node_count what exists; a node owning a nested graph (composite / macro instance) carries "subgraph" with the name to pass back as graph_name. With node_id, nodes holds that one node (nodes[0]) and node_count is 1.`

## `get_property_access_path`

*Read-only.*

Read a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path -- the anim-Blueprint property binding (InAnimInstance.Foo, InDeltaTime...) that no ordinary pin read exposes -- as segments plus its display text_path, and say whether the leaf actually RESOLVED (a still-wildcard Value pin means the path points at nothing). Read-only; errors on any node that is not a K2Node_PropertyAccess. Writer twin: set_property_access_path.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint). |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the property-access node (from get_graph_nodes). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, graph_name, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin:{name,direction,type,...} } -- resolved:false (Value pin still wildcard) is the signal that the binding is broken.`

## `implement_interface`

*Destructive.*

Add a Blueprint Interface to a Blueprint's implemented list (asset path or class name). NOT idempotent: an interface already implemented comes back as an error, unlike remove_interface. It only registers the contract -- the graphs that IMPLEMENT each member are created by add_blueprint_function with override=true, which is also the only correct route for interface EVENTS.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `interface_path` | string | yes | Blueprint interface asset path (e.g. /Game/Dir/BPI_Foo.BPI_Foo), or a resolvable interface class name/path |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, interface, implemented } -- implemented is always true on success; failure is an error response. Confirm the member set with get_blueprint_functions (interface graphs live in ImplementedInterfaces, not FunctionGraphs).`

## `lint_blueprint_graph`

*Read-only.*

Read-only lint of a Blueprint's graphs for four authoring bugs that COMPILE CLEAN and only show up in play: eclipsed_interface_event and custom_event_shadowing_override (a node that looks like an override and is not, so the base contract never runs), unreachable_exec_node (a node no exec chain reaches from any entry) and function_exit_without_return (a live exec path that falls off the end of a value-returning function, so the caller silently gets false/0/None). Scans ALL ubergraph + function + macro graphs by default. HONESTY LIMIT: findings:[] is NOT a clean bill of health -- by deliberate design it never flags a merely unconnected exec output, so a Branch or Is Valid with dangling outputs can pass; check linked_to yourself with get_graph_nodes (compact=false, or node_id for one node).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint to analyze. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Optional single graph to analyze; when omitted, scans ALL ubergraph (event) pages + function graphs + macro graphs owned by this Blueprint. Interface-override graphs are NOT in that default set -- name one explicitly to lint it. |

**Returns:** `{ findings: [ { kind, node_id, node_title, graph_name, why, fix_hint, pin? } ] } -- kind is one of eclipsed_interface_event, custom_event_shadowing_override, unreachable_exec_node, function_exit_without_return (this one also reports the offending exec pin in "pin"); "why" carries a best-effort pointer at the likely upstream break. No counters and no coverage flags: an empty array only means these four rules found nothing.`

## `list_editor_utility_widgets`

*Read-only.*

List the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint assets under a content folder and its subfolders, read from the Asset Registry without loading them. Returns search_path, count and widgets [{name, asset_path, package_name, package_path}]; open one as an editor tab with run_editor_utility_widget.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | Content folder to search recursively, without a trailing slash, e.g. "/Game/EditorUtilities" (default /Game). |

**Returns:** `{ name, asset_path, package_name, package_path, search_path, count, widgets }`

## `list_overridable_functions`

*Read-only.*

Enumerate the functions/events that a Blueprint deriving from a class could override. Works on an EXISTING Blueprint (blueprint_name) or on ANY class (class_name) so the override surface can be inspected BEFORE the child exists. Gated with UEdGraphSchema_K2::CanKismetOverrideFunction -- the same predicate add_blueprint_function(override=true) enforces -- so discovery and authoring agree (a bare NativeEvent||FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter lets a parent Blueprint's *__DelegateSignature through as "overridable"). Each entry reports where the member is DECLARED and where it is last IMPLEMENTED, with is_stub, which is what distinguishes a concrete ancestor from its `_Abstract` sibling.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | no | Name/path of an existing Blueprint. Its ParentClass is the override surface. |
| `class_name` | string | no | Alternative to blueprint_name: any class ("Actor", "/Script/Engine.Pawn", "/Game/.../BP_X.BP_X_C", or a Blueprint asset path). The override surface is THAT class, i.e. what a new child would get. Ignored when blueprint_name is given. |
| `include_non_overridable` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). true also lists the entries a NativeEvent\|\|FUNC_BlueprintEvent filter passes but CanKismetOverrideFunction rejects (delegate signatures, BlueprintInternalUseOnly, deprecated), each flagged can_kismet_override=false. Nothing is lost silently. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name?, class_name?, source_mode, resolved_class, base_class, ancestors: [string], count, functions: [{ function_name, display_name, declaring_class, is_native_event, is_event, is_interface, interface_name?, kind, can_kismet_override, has_override_graph, has_user_logic, is_implemented, parent_impl_kind, parent_impl_owner_class, parent_impl_graph, parent_impl_node_count, is_stub, is_stub_basis }] }`

## `list_scripted_action_utilities`

*Read-only.*

List the Editor Utility Blueprints under a content folder (subfolders included) whose class derives from UAssetActionUtility (kind asset: Content Browser right-click actions) or UActorActionUtility (kind actor: level actor actions). Each Editor Utility Blueprint found is LOADED to test its class, so a large folder is slow; plain Blueprints and Editor Utility Widgets are not listed. Read-only; a folder with none, or one that does not exist, is an empty list, not an error. Run one with run_asset_action_utility, which also lists its CallInEditor actions; create one with create_editor_utility_blueprint (parent_class "AssetActionUtility" or "ActorActionUtility"); Editor Utility Widgets: list_editor_utility_widgets.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | no | Content folder to search, subfolders included, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools", without a trailing slash (default /Game). |

**Returns:** `{ search_path: string, count: int, utilities: [{ name: string, path: string, package_name: string, kind: string, parent_class: string }] }`

## `list_widget_bound_events`

*Read-only.*

List every event-dispatcher BINDING wired in a Blueprint, across the three node kinds that make one in practice: UK2Node_AddDelegate (from add_object_bound_event / add_graph_node node_type="add_delegate"), UK2Node_ComponentBoundEvent (from add_component_bound_event -- a component's dispatcher OR a UMG widget's, e.g. a Button's OnClicked) and UK2Node_ActorBoundEvent (a level actor's, bound from the Level Blueprint). Each entry reports which kind it is (binding_kind), what it is bound ON (bound_to: the component/widget variable, or the actor), the delegate's owner class and name, and the handler on the other end. Despite the name it works on ANY Blueprint -- but it only walks Ubergraph pages and FunctionGraphs, so a binding inside a macro or interface graph is out of scope. Run it BEFORE add_object_bound_event / add_component_bound_event: double-binding one delegate to two handlers compiles fine and silently runs BOTH. A reader that cannot see what the writer wrote is worse than no reader: a 0 reads as "not wired" and sends you to re-wire what is already there.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path (Actor Blueprint, Widget Blueprint or Level Blueprint). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, bindings:[{ graph_name, node_id, binding_kind, bound_to, delegate_owner_class, delegate_name, delegate_resolved, wired, custom_event_name, custom_event_node_id }], binding_count, kind_counts:{add_delegate,component_bound_event,actor_bound_event} } -- binding_kind names the node class behind the entry. bound_to is the component/widget variable name (component_bound_event), the actor name (actor_bound_event), or empty for add_delegate, whose target pin is left unconnected by design. delegate_resolved=false means the delegate no longer resolves live (renamed/removed). wired=false is a DANGLING add_delegate bind (its Delegate pin has no handler); the two *BoundEvent kinds ARE their own handler, so they are always wired and custom_event_name is the generated BndEvt__ function.`

## `move_node`

*Destructive.*

Move a node to a new [x, y] canvas position. Purely cosmetic layout: no pin, link, default or type changes, and no compile. Returns the position actually applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node to move |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |
| `position_x` | number | no | Node X position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `position_y` | number | no | Node Y position on the graph canvas (ignored when node_position is set) |
| `node_position` | array | no | Node canvas position as [x, y]; takes precedence over position_x/position_y |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pos_x, pos_y }`

## `recombine_blueprint_pin`

*Destructive.*

Collapse a previously split struct pin back into ONE pin (inverse of split_blueprint_pin), which is what set_pin_default_value needs before it will write a struct literal. Accepts either the parent pin's name or any of its sub-pin names; links on the sub-pins are dropped by the engine as part of recombining.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node owning the pin. |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | Name of the parent pin OR of any of its sub-pins. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ recombined } -- always true on the success path; a pin that is not split is an error response instead.`

## `reconcile_function_signature`

*Destructive.*

Repair a LOCAL function graph's parameter pins so they match a parent UFUNCTION -- for an override whose signature went stale after a reparent -- WITHOUT nuking the graph's downstream nodes, which is what re-creating the override by hand costs you. It diffs the parent's parameters against the function's entry/result pins: mode='add_missing' (the default) only ADDS the missing pins, so it is non-destructive and safe to run blind; mode='remove_extra' / 'mirror' also DROP pins the parent lacks, which can sever downstream connections, and are therefore gated behind force_remove=true -- without it the extra pins are merely REPORTED (partially_implemented=true).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path owning the function. |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the local function graph to reconcile. |
| `parent_class` | string | no | Optional: class whose UFUNCTION defines the target signature (default: the Blueprint's current ParentClass). |
| `mode` | string | no | Optional (default 'add_missing'): 'add_missing' \| 'remove_extra' \| 'mirror'. |
| `force_remove` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): actually remove extra pins for 'remove_extra'/'mirror' (may drop connections). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, parent_class, mode, added:[{name,direction}], removed:[{name,direction}], extra_pins:[{name,direction}], missing_pins:[{name,direction}], removal_performed, partially_implemented, note, success }`

## `remove_blueprint_function`

*Destructive.*

Delete a function graph OWNED BY the Blueprint (Blueprint->FunctionGraphs) by name. WARNING: It resolves more graphs than it can delete: name lookup goes through FindGraph (all graphs, interface overrides and macros included) but the delete only touches FunctionGraphs and only when bAllowDeletion is true, so an INTERFACE OVERRIDE resolves and cannot be removed. That case is a hard error naming the reason -- to change an interface override, author the signature on the INTERFACE and re-create it (add_function_parameter on the BPI_ -> compile_blueprint -> add_blueprint_function with override=true). Not idempotent: a name that does not resolve is an error. TRAP when deleting to re-create: the class is NOT regenerated here, so an immediate add_blueprint_function with the same name fails with "is an inherited overridable function (declared on &lt;this very class>)" because the stale UFunction is still in the generated class -- put a compile_blueprint BETWEEN the two calls. Callers of the removed function are left broken until the next compile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the function graph to remove; must exist, be owned by this Blueprint and be deletable, or the call errors |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, removed_function: string, success: bool } -- success:true means the graph is gone from Blueprint->FunctionGraphs (re-read after the delete), not merely that the call ran.`

## `remove_component_from_blueprint`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove one or more component nodes from a Blueprint's SCS, with a DOUBLE CENSUS (flat AllNodes vs a walk of RootNodes) so collateral losses are reported instead of hidden: also_removed names descendants that went with their parent and unexpected_losses names nodes left in AllNodes but unreachable from any root. Batch-capable and that is the point -- chaining SINGLE-node calls on the same Blueprint is exactly the pattern that deletes components nobody asked for, so pass component_names and take ONE compile for the lot. A re-added component comes back with its CLASS defaults: per-instance overrides are gone and do not come back on save. IDEMPOTENT, so it is safe in scripts that re-run: a requested component that is not there is listed in not_found, and when none of them is there the call still succeeds with already_removed:true and nothing removed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name/path of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | no | Name of the component to remove (single form; matches the variable name or the _GEN_VARIABLE internal name) |
| `component_names` | array | no | Optional array of component names removed as ONE batch with a SINGLE compile. Chaining single-node calls is the pattern that causes collateral deletions. Merged with component_name when both are given. |
| `promote_children` | boolean | no | Optional bool, default true: keep descendants by re-parenting them (RemoveNodeAndPromoteChildren). Pass false for plain RemoveNode, which orphans the whole subtree. |

**Returns:** `{ success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, removed_component, component_name, removed, already_removed, requested[], removed_components[], also_removed[], unexpected_losses[], not_found[], still_present[], node_count_before, node_count_after, reachable_before, reachable_after, orphans_before[], orphans_after[], root_nodes_before[], root_nodes_after[], root_nodes_changed, promote_children, compiled, compile_count, success, verification } } -- removed: at least one node went; already_removed: none of the requested names was there (a no-op, not an error).`

## `remove_event_dispatcher`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove an event dispatcher, dropping BOTH artifacts add_event_dispatcher created: the delegate member variable AND its signature graph (delete_blueprint_variable removes only the variable and strands the graph, which is why this exists). Idempotent -- when neither artifact is present it returns removed:false instead of erroring. Broadcast/bind nodes that referenced it are left broken: compile_blueprint with return_messages=true after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `dispatcher_name` | string | yes | Name of the event dispatcher to remove (must be one this Blueprint owns; inherited ones have no local artifacts) |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, removed } -- removed:false means nothing was there (no-op), not a failure.`

## `remove_interface`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove an implemented Blueprint Interface (inverse of implement_interface) and, unless preserve_functions is set, DELETE the graphs that implemented it -- work is lost, so pass preserve_functions=true to keep them as ordinary Blueprint functions. Idempotent, unlike implement_interface: an interface that is not implemented returns removed:false instead of erroring.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `interface_path` | string | yes | Blueprint interface asset path (or class name) to remove |
| `preserve_functions` | boolean | no | When true, keep the interface's function graphs as normal Blueprint functions instead of deleting them; defaults to false |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, interface, removed } -- removed:false means it was not implemented (no-op), not a failure.`

## `remove_unused_variables`

*Destructive.*

Delete EVERY variable the engine considers unused from a Blueprint in one shot (GatherUnusedVariables + RemoveUnusedVariables) and report which ones went. Destructive and non-selective -- "unused" means no graph node reads or writes it, so a variable only touched from C++, a DataTable, a save game or a runtime name lookup counts as unused and is deleted. Preview it by comparing get_blueprint_variables before/after, or delete a specific one with delete_blueprint_variable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name: string, removed_count: int, removed_variables?: [string] } -- removed_variables is the list gathered BEFORE the removal and removed_count what the engine reported removing; when they disagree, trust neither and re-read get_blueprint_variables.`

## `rename_blueprint_variable`

*Destructive.*

Rename a member variable DECLARED on this Blueprint, KEEPING everything the delete+re-add workaround throws away: the VarGuid, the type, the default value, the category, the tooltip and the replication flags -- and, crucially, RE-WIRING every Get/Set node that reads it, in this Blueprint and in every dependent one. This is the only correct way to rename an authored variable in place (e.g. to translate its name). WARNING: it refuses a variable that has a RepNotify function: the engine's own rename opens a MODAL dialog for that case (FSuppressableWarningDialog, which does NOT honour unattended mode) and would hang the editor waiting for a click -- clear the RepNotify with set_blueprint_variable_replication, rename, then set it back. WARNING: dependent Blueprints are only repaired if they are LOADED: this command loads the ones the Asset Registry reports as referencers first, and reports them in `referencers_loaded`, but an asset that references it in a way the registry does not see keeps the old name silently. It does NOT create CoreRedirects, so a saved game, a DataTable cell or a Python set_editor_property that names the variable as text is NOT fixed -- grep for those. Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every referencer.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path owning the variable. |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint; inherited/native ones are refused. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New name. Must be a legal identifier and free across the WHOLE class chain (the engine does not check this and would happily create a duplicate). Case-only changes are allowed. |
| `load_referencers` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so the engine's reference fixup reaches them; it only ever sees what is already in memory. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, old_name, new_name, renamed (re-read: true only if new_name exists and old_name is gone), referencers_loaded: [string], repnotify_cleared: bool, warning? }`

## `rename_function_parameter`

*Destructive.*

Rename a PARAMETER of a Blueprint function graph -- the parameter counterpart of rename_blueprint_variable, and the only headless way to do it: add_function_parameter only ADDS, there is no remove_function_parameter, so "delete and re-add" is not even available. It renames the pin on the Entry node and on EVERY Result node of the graph, and registers a CoreRedirect so that call sites re-map themselves. That redirect is not a nicety: it is what stops this from being a PHANTOM PIN FACTORY. With the redirect, the call site's pin takes the new name AND KEEPS ITS LITERAL VALUE; renamed WITHOUT one, the old pin stays alive and ORPHANED on the caller. WARNING: that orphan is silent: it survives compiles that report num_errors:0 -- so `compile_blueprint` is NOT the oracle here. The oracle is get_graph_nodes(compact=false) on the callers, checking that NO pin still carries the old name. The redirect matches on `Class.Function.Param`, so it reaches callers that merely CALL the function (K2Node_Message included) without implementing its interface, and dependents that are not even loaded -- both of which rename_blueprint_variable cannot reach. It does NOT rename anything that names the parameter as TEXT (a DataTable cell, a saved game, Python). Run compile_blueprint afterwards and save_asset on this Blueprint AND on every caller. AND THE COMPILE IS NOT THE END OF IT: what reaches the .uasset is UserDefinedPins, not the EdGraphPins you read back -- a rename checked only on the latter can report renamed:true, compile at num_errors:0, be saved and COMMITTED, and still come back as the OLD name the next time the editor starts. So it also reports entry_user_pins_after/result_user_pins_after (the serialized side, legitimately EMPTY on an interface-override graph) and refuses to claim success while any UserDefinedPin still carries the old name. The end-to-end oracle is still disk: save_asset -> reload_asset_package -> get_function_pins.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path owning the function graph. |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the function graph (an interface's own function graph and an interface-override graph both work). |
| `old_name` | string | yes | Current parameter name, matched on the Entry node and on every Result node. A name present on only one of them is fine. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New parameter name. Must be free on the terminal nodes; a collision is refused up front via the engine's own dry-run, before anything is touched. |
| `write_redirect` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Also PERSIST the redirect as a +PropertyRedirects line in Config/DefaultEngine.ini, so it survives a restart and reaches the other machine. With false the redirect is registered in memory only and the rename EVAPORATES for anyone who opens the project later. |
| `load_referencers` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Load the Blueprints the Asset Registry lists as referencers BEFORE renaming, so their nodes reconstruct in this session instead of the next one. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, old_name, new_name, renamed: bool, terminals_renamed: [string], entry_pins_after: [string], result_pins_after: [string], entry_user_pins_after: [string], result_user_pins_after: [string], redirect_registered: string, redirect_persisted_to: string|null, referencers_loaded: [string], must_compile_and_save: [string], warning: string } -- the *_user_pins_after pair is the SERIALIZED side (UserDefinedPins): empty on an interface-override graph is normal, but the old name appearing there is the rename that will revert on restart.`

## `reparent_blueprint`

*Destructive.*

Change a Blueprint's parent class, guarded and rollback-capable; asking for the parent it already has is a no-op (reparented:false), not an error. On top of the reparent itself it takes: a pre-flight snapshot (parent chain, own-variable count, CDO component count); an OPTIONAL variable de-collision rename (rename_colliding_vars) for own variables whose name collides with a member the NEW parent already declares, which a plain reparent would otherwise clobber; the delta-serialization compile flags, without which a Blueprint with more than ~10 type-pinned variables CRASHES the editor during reinstancing; the same SCS-root reconciliation the Blueprint editor itself does, so a silently renamed component ("Mesh" -> "Mesh1") is reported instead of hidden; an invariant post-check (parent matches, no compile error, own-variable count did not shrink); and, on failure, an in-memory auto_rollback that restores the original parent, restores the component names and recompiles (auto_rollback=false leaves a failed reparent in place). It never saves to disk. This is a genuinely destructive multi-step transaction: run it with dry_run=true first on any real fork -- that reports the plan and the would-rename set without mutating anything.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path to reparent. |
| `new_parent_class` | string | yes | New parent class name or path (native /Script, /Game/.../BP.BP_C, or a BP asset path -> its GeneratedClass). |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): analyze + report the plan (snapshot, would-rename vars, component collisions) without mutating. |
| `rename_colliding_vars` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): before reparenting, rename own NewVariables that collide by name with a member on the new parent. |
| `auto_rollback` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): on post-check failure, restore the original parent, restore the SCS node names and recompile. |
| `reconcile_scene_root` | boolean | no | Optional (default true): run the editor's own post-reparent conform pass -- ValidateSceneRootNodes + PrepareToConformSparseClassData + a second pass after the compile. Setting it FALSE disables all three; it exists only as a bisect escape hatch. |
| `treat_component_renames_as_regression` | boolean | no | Optional (default false): count a silently renamed SCS component as a post-check regression (which triggers auto_rollback). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, blueprint_path, old_parent, new_parent, dry_run, reparented, renamed_variables:[{from,to}], pre_variable_count, post_variable_count, pre_component_count, post_component_count, pre_scs_node_count, post_scs_node_count, scene_root_reconciled, scene_root_reconciled_post_compile, default_scene_root_removed, sparse_class_data_conform_prepared, compile_messages:[{severity,text}], compile_error_count, compile_warning_count, renamed_components:[{guid,from,to,matched_by}], removed_components:[{guid,name}], components_without_guid, colliding_components:[{name,own_class,parent_class}], child_only_components:[{name,class}], compile_status, parent_match, compile_ok, variables_intact, components_intact, post_check_ok, rolled_back, rollback_complete, rollback_restored_components:[{guid,name}] (snapshotted nodes whose name MATCHES again after the rollback), rollback_unrestored_components:[{guid,expected_name,actual_name}], rollback_compile_messages:[{severity,text}], regressions:[string], saved_to_disk (always false -- this tool never saves), persistence_note, verification, verification_checks, success }`

## `run_asset_action_utility`

*Destructive.*

Invoke one CallInEditor action of a scripted Asset or Actor Action Utility Blueprint (by asset path) on a new transient instance of its class, as the right-click menu does but with no Content Browser or level selection. function_name picks the action, case-insensitive, else the first one found; the reply always lists every action in action_functions. Only a parameterless action runs: one that takes parameters, a name that matches no action, a utility with no actions or an abstract utility class is a success with invoked=false and a note saying why. What the action does is up to its Blueprint; this tool saves nothing itself. A missing asset, one that is not a Blueprint, or a Blueprint that is not an Asset/Actor Action Utility is an error. Find them with list_scripted_action_utilities; create one with create_editor_utility_blueprint (parent_class "AssetActionUtility" or "ActorActionUtility").

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `utility_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the utility Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools/EUA_RenameTextures" (the object path form also works). |
| `function_name` | string | no | Name of the CallInEditor action to run, case-insensitive; when absent the first action found on the class runs. |

**Returns:** `{ utility_path, kind, generated_class, action_functions, function_name, function_found, invoked, note }`

## `run_editor_utility_widget`

*Destructive.*

Open an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint (by asset path) as an editor tab through UEditorUtilitySubsystem: register its tab spawner and invoke the tab, which creates the widget and so runs whatever its Blueprint does on construct. The tab ID is the asset path plus _ActiveTab, so a repeat call brings back the same tab instead of adding a second one. Nothing is saved. widget_spawned is false when no live widget came back; in a commandlet nothing is registered and tab_id is empty. A missing asset, or one that is not an Editor Utility Widget Blueprint, is an error. Create one with create_editor_utility_widget_blueprint; find them with list_editor_utility_widgets; right-click actions: run_asset_action_utility.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `widget_blueprint_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Editor Utility Widget Blueprint, e.g. "/Game/EditorTools/EUW_Tools" (the object path form also works). |

**Returns:** `{ widget_blueprint_path, asset_path, tab_id, registration_name, registered, tab_exists, widget_spawned }`

## `set_blueprint_class_replication`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set class-level ACTOR replication on a Blueprint's CDO (bReplicates, optionally bAlwaysRelevant), compile, and read the values back off the RE-FETCHED post-compile CDO. Actor Blueprints only: a component Blueprint is refused (component replication is set_component_replication). Related reader trap: audit_replication's class_replicates reads the ACTOR flag, so it reports false for every component Blueprint whatever its CDO says.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of an Actor Blueprint (must be compiled at least once). |
| `replicates` | boolean | yes | Whether the Actor class replicates to network clients. Required. |
| `always_relevant` | boolean | no | Sets the Actor's bAlwaysRelevant flag; only applied when the field is present |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, replicates, always_relevant_set, always_relevant } -- values re-read from the CDO after compiling; always_relevant is only present when it was requested.`

## `set_blueprint_component_array_element`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Author ONE element of a TArray property on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS, or ICH-aware for a component inherited from an ancestor Blueprint): patch named struct members of an existing element, insert a new element at an index, or remove one. Every OTHER element is exported before and after and compared, so a whole-array rewrite that quietly loses the empty/None gaps cannot pass itself off as a targeted edit. There is deliberately NO 'move' operation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset path or short name |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component variable name (own or inherited) |
| `property_name` | string | yes | Name of the TArray property on the component template |
| `index` | number | yes | 0-based element index. set_fields/remove need an existing index; insert accepts 0..Num (Num appends) |
| `operation` | string | no | 'set_fields' (default), 'insert' or 'remove' |
| `fields` | object | no | Object of { StructMemberName: value } applied to the element. Used by set_fields, and by insert when the element type is a struct |
| `element` | any | no | Whole-element JSON value. Used by insert for NON-struct element types (or instead of 'fields' for a struct) |
| `compile` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): compile so the edited template reinstances |
| `save` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): save the Blueprint package after the compile |

**Returns:** `{ success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, property_name, source, operation, index, inner_type, num_before, num_after, fields_applied[], field_errors[], siblings_unchanged, siblings_changed[], element_value, post_compile_num, post_compile_element, compiled, saved, save_error?, verification } }`

## `set_blueprint_component_collision`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set collision on a Blueprint component TEMPLATE (own SCS or inherited via ICH), not on a spawned actor, applying in this order: `profile` through SetCollisionProfileName (which expands the profile into the FBodyInstance response array -- a raw reflection write would set the string and leave BodyInstance inconsistent, and that is the whole reason this is a separate tool), then `collision_enabled`, then per-channel `responses`. Use it instead of set_blueprint_component_properties for anything collision-shaped. Unknown channel, response or collision_enabled names are hard errors, never a silent default. Note the ORDER: a later profile would reset the per-channel responses, so responses always win here.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset path or name (required) |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component to modify (required); must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors with "no collision to set" |
| `profile` | string | no | Collision profile name, e.g. "BlockAll" (optional). Applied FIRST, so it does not undo the per-channel responses below. |
| `collision_enabled` | string | no | ECollisionEnabled value name: NoCollision, QueryOnly, PhysicsOnly or QueryAndPhysics (optional). Any other string is an error. |
| `responses` | object | no | Object mapping channel -> response, e.g. {"Visibility":"Ignore","ECC_Pawn":"Overlap"} (optional). Channels accept the friendly display name or an ECC_* token (custom project channels included); responses are Ignore, Overlap or Block. An unknown channel is refused rather than defaulting to WorldStatic. |
| `compile` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default FALSE): compile the Blueprint afterwards so the FBodyInstance change reinstances on the next spawn/PIE. Without it the edit stays in the uncompiled template. |
| `return_messages` | boolean | no | No effect here: it is only read by the compile this tool may run internally, whose message log is discarded. Call compile_blueprint directly if you want the messages. |

**Returns:** `{ success, data: { blueprint_name, component_name, source ("scs" | "inherited-ich" | "inherited-native": which template was written), profile?, collision_enabled?, responses_applied: [{channel, response}], compiled } } -- responses_applied lists ONLY the per-channel writes; profile and collision_enabled appear as their own fields only when they were given. Nothing is re-read: verify with get_blueprint_component_property or get_collision_info.`

## `set_blueprint_component_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the DEFAULT of one or several properties on Blueprint component TEMPLATES -- own SCS components, ones INHERITED from a parent Blueprint (written as an InheritableComponentHandler override) and native subobjects -- with ONE compile and ONE save, then verify each value on the post-compile template. Use it for component templates: set_properties neither creates an inherited override nor compiles or saves; set_component_property edits placed actors. One write: component_name + property_name + property_value; several: overrides[]. TRAPS behind a green reply: (1) it can drop another component IN MEMORY -- count get_blueprint_components before and after, cure with reload_asset_package(on_dirty="discard"); (2) an object-reference write can land None and still report override_persisted:true -- check get_blueprint_component_overrides; (3) actors already placed keep their serialized value. Collision: set_blueprint_component_collision; override-free read: get_blueprint_component_property.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset path or short name |
| `overrides` | array | no | Optional array of { component_name, property_name, property_value } objects, applied in the given order. Required unless the single-write form (component_name + property_name + property_value) is given; both together apply overrides[] first, then the single write. |
| `component_name` | string | no | Optional single-write form: component variable name (own or inherited). Needs property_name and property_value too. |
| `property_name` | string | no | Optional single-write form: property to set on that component template. |
| `property_value` | any | no | Optional single-write form: the new value (any JSON type; same importer as set_component_property). An array value REWRITES THE WHOLE ARRAY, including the empty/None gaps -- set_blueprint_component_array_element edits one element and proves the siblings did not move. |
| `compile` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). false skips the compile: nothing is verifiable, every entry reports matches_requested=false with verification_status='not_verifiable' |
| `save` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true). Saves the Blueprint package ONCE, after the compile |

**Returns:** `{ success, error?, data: { blueprint_name, requested_count, applied_count, verified_count, mismatched_count, failed_count, compiled, saved, save_error?, equality_predicate, results: [{ index, component_name, property_name, source, component_class, override_persisted, applied, apply_error?, verification_status, matches_requested, post_value, post_source, note? }], verification } } -- source tells which template was hit (scs / inherited-ich / inherited-scs / inherited-native); component_class is that template's class, read before the compile; override_persisted is false only when an inherited-ich override did not survive the compile.`

## `set_blueprint_function_pure`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Mark a Blueprint function as PURE (or back to impure), the editor's "Pure" checkbox: a pure function has no exec pins and is re-evaluated wherever its output is read. REQUIRED to finish a UMG property binding -- FDelegateEditorBinding::IsBindingValid refuses any function that is not FUNC_BlueprintPure or const, so add_widget_property_binding will report valid:false until this has been run on the function. The counterpart reader is get_blueprint_functions's is_pure, which reads the same flag off the same UK2Node_FunctionEntry. WARNING: Turning a function pure REMOVES its exec pins: any existing wire into or out of them is dropped by the reconstruct, so do this BEFORE building the function's body, not after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint owning the function. |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of the function GRAPH (not an event; events cannot be pure). |
| `is_pure` | boolean | no | true to mark pure (default true), false to make it impure again. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, is_pure, was_pure, changed, function_flags } -- is_pure is RE-READ from the entry node after the compile, so it is evidence and not an echo.`

## `set_blueprint_function_rpc`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn a Blueprint FUNCTION into an RPC (rpc_type Server / Client / NetMulticast, or NotReplicated to undo it, plus reliable), then compile and read the FUNC_Net* flags back off the entry node. This is the ONLY headless way to author an RPC THAT TAKES ARGUMENTS: add_function_parameter cannot reach a custom event, so build the RPC as add_blueprint_function -> compile_blueprint -> add_function_parameter -> here. Engine limits that follow: a replicated function cannot return a value and cannot host latent nodes (put a Delay in a separate, parameterless custom event).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint. |
| `function_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing FUNCTION graph on the Blueprint (a custom event has no entry node here and is refused). |
| `rpc_type` | string | yes | One of "NotReplicated", "Server", "Client", "NetMulticast" (case-insensitive). |
| `reliable` | boolean | no | Mark the RPC reliable; ignored (and cleared) when rpc_type is NotReplicated; defaults to false |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, function_name, rpc_type, is_net, reliable, function_flags } -- re-read from the entry node's flags after compiling; rpc_type is the RESOLVED type, so compare it with what you asked for. Proof that the call really crosses the wire is not here: drive it in PIE and read the resulting state on the OTHER side.`

## `set_blueprint_variable_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint: writes the live CDO and mirrors the result back into the serialized variable description so it survives save/reload. LIMIT (not a lie, a hard boundary): it CANNOT touch an INHERITED variable -- it answers "Variable 'X' is not declared on this blueprint" -- so the "child that only overrides a parent default" pattern needs the CDO route (execute_python + set_editor_property + compile_blueprint + save). And on a class with actors already placed in a level, the placed instances keep their serialized value: verify on the instances, never on the CDO.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused) |
| `value` | string | no | New default in exported-text form, parsed into the variable's type; empty allowed. A value the type cannot parse is an error AND the previous value is restored (the engine's struct import zeroes the target before parsing, so a failed parse wipes the CDO). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, default_value, roundtrip_verified } -- default_value is re-exported from the CDO after the write, so it is the real stored value. WARNING: roundtrip_verified:false means the exported text does NOT re-import into the type (e.g. FGameplayTagContainer): the CDO holds the right value and the compiler's property copy carries it, but the serialized description was deliberately left empty because feeding an unparseable string back through a Full compile ZEROES the default. Verify that variable on the CDO after compiling, and prefer wiring it in the graph if it must survive a fresh regeneration.`

## `set_blueprint_variable_metadata`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the editor-facing checkboxes and text of an existing Blueprint variable: instance_editable (per-instance editability), save_game (CPF_SaveGame -- whether the variable goes into a .sav), expose_on_spawn (adds the variable as a pin on SpawnActor), category and tooltip. Only the fields present are touched; passing none is an error. This is the fix for a variable created by add_blueprint_variable, which is born NOT instance-editable while the readers report it as editable. Variable must be declared on THIS Blueprint; on a library variable the answer is a child class of your own, not this call. WARNING: this call does NOT compile: it structurally-modifies the Blueprint, which regenerates the SKELETON only, so a save_game just written is authored but NOT yet on the generated class the save archive reads -- the response says so in save_game_needs_compile, and the loop that finishes the job is compile_blueprint -> save_asset -> get_blueprint_variable_detailed_info and check save_game_generated.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable declared on THIS Blueprint (inherited ones are refused). |
| `instance_editable` | boolean | no | true = editable on each placed actor. Verify by WRITING the placed instance and reading it back; the reporting field is unreliable for every variable. |
| `save_game` | boolean | no | true = tick "SaveGame" (CPF_SaveGame), so a SaveGame archive (ArIsSaveGame) serializes this variable; false unticks it. The only headless way to set this flag -- set_properties, Python, set_blueprint_variable_replication and BlueprintEditorLibrary all refuse it. Needs a compile to reach the generated class. |
| `expose_on_spawn` | boolean | no | true = the variable shows up as an input pin on SpawnActorFromClass. Verify on the NODE's pins, not on get_blueprint_variables' expose_on_spawn, which reports false for variables that ARE exposed. |
| `category` | string | no | Category to group the variable under in the editor |
| `tooltip` | string | no | Tooltip text shown for the variable |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, updated, save_game?, save_game_generated?, save_game_needs_compile? } -- updated:true only means at least one field was applied, not that it persisted. The three save_game_* fields appear only when save_game was passed, and are READ BACK after the write: save_game off the variable descriptor, save_game_generated off the FProperty of the generated class.`

## `set_blueprint_variable_replication`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a Blueprint variable's replication mode -- None / Replicated / RepNotify (RepNotify also creates the OnRep_&lt;Variable> function graph if missing) -- then compiles and reads CPF_Net/CPF_RepNotify back. TRAP: the full green report can come back WITHOUT the flag surviving into the generated class (a variable reported is_replicated:true that never replicates; re-running this same call fixes it). The ground truth is audit_replication (its payload's replicated_variables list), then compile and re-audit -- never this return, and never one client alone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint. |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited/native variables are refused). |
| `mode` | string | yes | One of "None", "Replicated", "RepNotify" (case-insensitive). "None" also clears the RepNotify function and resets the lifetime condition. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, mode, is_replicated, is_rep_notify, rep_notify_func, property_flags } -- read back from the variable's flags after compiling, which is necessary but NOT sufficient (see the trap above).`

## `set_component_replication`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set bReplicates on ONE SCS component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (the archetype, not a spawned actor's instance), compile, and read it back off the template. It governs the component's own PROPERTY replication; note that a component declared in the SCS already routes its RPCs through its stable network name WITHOUT this flag (a component added at RUNTIME does not, and loses them). For the owning actor use set_blueprint_class_replication.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name (or full object path) of the Blueprint. |
| `component_name` | string | yes | SCS component variable name on this Blueprint (inherited-only components have no local SCS node and are not found). |
| `replicates` | boolean | yes | Whether the component should replicate. Required. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, component_name, replicates } -- replicates is re-read from the template after compiling.`

## `set_event_dispatcher_signature`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add to (mode="add", the idempotent default) or rewrite (mode="replace") the parameter list of a dispatcher this Blueprint OWNS -- inherited dispatchers have no local signature graph and are refused with the list of owned ones. Every requested type is resolved BEFORE anything is mutated, so a bad type aborts cleanly. The parameters become the OUTPUT pins of every bound handler and the INPUT pins of add_broadcast_node; existing nodes keep stale pins until compile_blueprint reconstructs them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path that OWNS the dispatcher (inherited dispatchers cannot be edited here). |
| `dispatcher_name` | string | yes | Name of an existing event dispatcher (created by add_event_dispatcher or the editor). |
| `params` | array | yes | Array of parameter specs to add: [ { name: string, type: string } ]. Dispatcher params are input-only; 'type' accepts the same strings as add_function_parameter (bool, int, int64, float, string, name, text, byte, Vector, Array&lt;T>, an object/class/struct/enum name or path). |
| `mode` | string | no | "add" (default, idempotent: skip a param whose name already exists) or "replace" (clear the existing signature first, then add the given params). |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, dispatcher_name, mode, added: [string], params: [ { name, type } ], param_count }`

## `set_mesh_material_color`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Tint one material slot of a Blueprint component template by creating a DYNAMIC material instance (MID) over the current or given material, setting one vector parameter, and assigning the MID to the slot. A MID is a RUNTIME object, so this is a quick preview, NOT the way to author a change that must survive save/reload -- for a persistent tint make a MaterialInstanceConstant and assign it with apply_material_to_blueprint. A parameter_name the material does not declare is accepted silently and simply does nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS component; must be a UPrimitiveComponent |
| `color` | array | yes | RGBA color [R, G, B, A] as floats, each clamped to 0.0-1.0; exactly 4 values are required |
| `material_slot` | number | no | Optional slot index; defaults to 0 |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional vector parameter name; defaults to "BaseColor". A name the material does not declare is NOT reported as an error -- it just has no visible effect. |
| `material_path` | string | no | Optional material asset path to use as the MID's parent; without it the component's current slot material is used, falling back to /Engine/BasicShapes/BasicShapeMaterial |

**Returns:** `{ component: string, material_slot: int, parameter_name: string, color: [number, number, number, number], success: bool } -- success:true only means the MID was created and assigned; re-read with get_blueprint_material_info after a save/reload to see whether anything persisted.`

## `set_physics_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set simulate-physics, mass override, linear and angular damping on ONE primitive component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node only -- inherited components are not found here, and it is the template, not a placed actor). Only the fields present are touched. It does NOT compile and does NOT save. For any other property of a component template use set_blueprint_component_properties, which is ICH-aware and reaches inherited components.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS component; must resolve to a UPrimitiveComponent or the call errors |
| `simulate_physics` | boolean | no | Optional bool to toggle physics simulation |
| `mass` | number | no | Optional mass override in kg (applied as SetMassOverrideInKg, not a scale) |
| `linear_damping` | number | no | Optional linear damping coefficient |
| `angular_damping` | number | no | Optional angular damping coefficient |

**Returns:** `{ component: string } -- just the component name back. NOTHING is read back, so verify with get_blueprint_component_property on each property you set.`

## `set_pin_default_value`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write the literal default of an UNCONNECTED input pin and return the value read BACK off the pin. Struct pins are canonicalized: a bare GameplayTag name becomes (TagName="X") and an UNREGISTERED tag is rejected up front instead of silently landing as an empty tag; value_json nativizes any struct (and is the only way to put SEVERAL tags in a GameplayTagContainer). Array/set/map pins are refused (use a MakeArray/MakeSet/MakeMap node) and so are pins currently split into sub-pins (recombine_blueprint_pin first). A plain string is fine for an FText pin. TRAP: on a FormatText "Format" pin the literal IS written but the {argument} pins are NOT created, leaving a valid, useless node -- build the string with Concat_StrStr / Conv_StringToText instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint asset name or path |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node owning the pin |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | Pin name; an INPUT pin of that name is preferred, any pin with the name is the fallback |
| `value` | string | no | Literal default in the pin's exported-text form; empty string allowed (clears it). For a struct pin, "()" clears and a leading "(" is passed through untouched. |
| `value_json` | object | no | Optional JSON object nativized into the struct's export-text form, for STRUCT pins only. For an FGameplayTagContainer it must carry a "GameplayTags" array (["A","B"] or [{"TagName":"A"}]) and every tag is validated; takes precedence over 'value'. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, pin_name, default_value } -- default_value is re-read from the pin AFTER the write, so it is the oracle for what actually landed (a rejected value shows up as the old one).`

## `set_property_access_path`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rewrite a UK2Node_PropertyAccess node's binding Path and reconstruct the node so the leaf property re-resolves and the Value pin re-types, then return the path READ BACK -- so resolved:true is real evidence the new binding points at something. It does NOT recompile: follow with compile_blueprint with return_messages=true. reconstructed:false means the PropertyAccessEditor feature was unavailable: the path WAS written but text_path/resolved_pin stay stale until the graph reopens.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path (usually an Animation Blueprint). |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the property-access node; any other node class is refused by name. |
| `path` | any | no | The new path: either an array of segment strings (["InAnimInstance","Foo"]) OR a dotted string ("InAnimInstance.Foo"). An empty result is an error, never a cleared binding. |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted. |

**Returns:** `{ node_id, graph_name, reconstructed, path:[string], text_path, resolved, resolved_pin, note? } -- path/text_path/resolved are re-read AFTER the reconstruct, so they are the oracle rather than an echo.`

## `set_replication_condition`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the ELifetimeCondition (COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly...) that decides WHICH clients get a replicated variable, then compile. It is the second half of set_blueprint_variable_replication, which decides WHETHER it replicates at all: on a variable that is not Replicated/RepNotify the condition is stored and completely INERT, and the response says so through is_replicated:false plus a "note". Blueprint-declared variables only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Name of a variable DECLARED on this Blueprint (inherited ones are refused). |
| `condition` | string | yes | ELifetimeCondition name, with or without the COND_ prefix (e.g. "OwnerOnly" or "COND_OwnerOnly"); an unknown name is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ blueprint_name, variable_name, condition, is_replicated, note? } -- condition is the canonical COND_ name that was stored; is_replicated:false means the setting has no effect yet.`

## `set_static_mesh_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Assign a static mesh asset and/or a slot-0 material to a mesh component TEMPLATE of a Blueprint (an OWN SCS node, not a placed actor) through the component's SetStaticMesh/SetMaterial. Does NOT compile and does NOT save; the reply reads the template back (static_mesh, material and a *_set flag for each). A path that does not load as a mesh or material, or a call with neither, fails with nothing changed. Use apply_material_to_blueprint when only a material is changing or the slot is not 0, and set_blueprint_component_properties for any other template property or an inherited component.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Name of an OWN SCS mesh component |
| `static_mesh` | string | no | Optional asset path of the UStaticMesh to assign; a path that does not load as a StaticMesh fails the call and nothing is changed |
| `material` | string | no | Optional asset path of the UMaterialInterface for slot 0; a path that does not load as a material fails the call and nothing is changed. At least one of static_mesh and material is required. |

**Returns:** `{ component: string, static_mesh: string, material: string, static_mesh_set: bool, material_set: bool } -- read back from the template: static_mesh is the mesh it holds and material its slot-0 material (the override, else the mesh's own), each an object path or "None"; <field>_set is true when that field was passed and the template now holds it. Nothing is compiled or saved.`

## `spawn_blueprint_actor`

*Additive.*

Spawn an instance of a Blueprint class as an actor and report WHICH world took it and whether the actor has AUTHORITY. Pick it for any Blueprint class; spawn_actor places the built-in engine types (StaticMeshActor, lights, CameraActor, Character), and the typed spawn_* tools place an engine class with its own fields. The default (world absent or 'editor') places it in the EDITOR level, not in play. For anything that must exist for every player during PIE use world='server'; world='pie' is ambiguous and can land on the CLIENT, where the actor has no authority, no AI controller and no server-side existence while looking identical in the payload. The actor is NOT saved into the map: save_level afterwards for an editor-world spawn.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Name of the blueprint |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label applied to the spawned actor (SetActorLabel); it is not the object name and is not made unique |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] world location |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'editor' (default) spawns into the editor level \| 'server' spawns into the PIE world WITH AUTHORITY (what you want for anything that must exist for every player: an actor spawned into the client world has no authority and no server-side existence) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context -- can land on the CLIENT) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') |

**Returns:** `{ actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, world: string, has_authority: bool (AActor::HasAuthority() read off the spawned actor), local_role: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `split_blueprint_pin`

*Destructive.*

Split a struct-typed pin (Vector, Rotator, Transform...) into its scalar sub-pins and return their names, so each component can be wired or defaulted on its own instead of writing the whole struct literal. Refused when the schema says the pin is not splittable. Note the interaction: set_pin_default_value REFUSES a pin that is currently split -- recombine_blueprint_pin first if you want to write the struct as one value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the node owning the pin. |
| `pin_name` | string | yes | Name of the struct pin to split (either direction). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ split, sub_pins:[string] } -- sub_pins are the names to pass to connect_pins / set_pin_default_value from now on (e.g. "NewLocation_X").`

## `validate_pin_connection`

*Read-only.*

Dry-run the K2 schema's verdict on a pin pair WITHOUT touching the graph: returns valid plus the schema's own message (which names the incompatible types) and its raw response code. connect_pins runs the same check and then connects, so use this one to test a plan before committing a build_blueprint_graph batch whose rollback can be refused, or to find out WHY a connection was rejected without leaving anything behind.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint_name` | string | yes | Blueprint name or path. |
| `source_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the source node. |
| `source_pin` | string | yes | Output pin name on the source node (falls back to any pin with that name). |
| `target_node_id` | string | yes | NodeGuid of the target node; must be in the same graph as the source. |
| `target_pin` | string | yes | Input pin name on the target node (falls back to any pin with that name). |
| `graph_name` | string | no | Target graph name; defaults to the Blueprint's event graph when omitted |

**Returns:** `{ valid, message, response_code } -- valid is false only for an outright DISALLOW; a response that would connect WITH a conversion node or by breaking an existing link still reports valid:true, and "message" is where that shows.`
